## Source: docs/native-patterns.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/native-patterns.md

# Native platform patterns and component imports

This prerelease Syntyr example uses original CSS, not upstream Blades source.
All patterns retain native HTML semantics and need **no runtime JavaScript**.
For a live static preview, see [the native recipe example (live alpha.5 source preview)](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/native-recipes.html).

## Native visibility is authoritative

Inside `.syn-root`, use the browser's `hidden` attribute to remove an element
from layout even when it also has `.syn-button`, `.syn-grid`, or semantic styles.
Syntyr's base layer preserves that native state. For find-in-page reveals, use
`hidden="until-found"`: the browser retains the element in layout and may
reveal it on search or fragment navigation. Use a layout-containing box:
do not force `display: none`, `display: inline`, or
`display: contents`. Those values prevent find-in-page reveal;
prefer a block, grid, or flex container. Do not replace these states with
`aria-hidden`, which does not hide an element visually or from keyboard focus.

## Native interaction recipes

The standard library includes the following **five native interaction
compositions**, using existing core classes plus normal HTML. They do **not**
require a new JavaScript runtime, Syntyr component subclass, or optional
`syntyr.native-recipes.css` import. Use `syntyr.core.css` for the classed
controls; load `syntyr.semantic.css` and opt in with `.syn-semantic` if
you want unclassed `meter` and `output` styling.

- **Exclusive accordion:** use `<details class="syn-details" name="faq">`
  and a real `<summary>` for each item. Reuse the `name` only *within*
  an intended disclosure group; only one item opens at once in current
  browsers. Do not invent `role="tab"`, `aria-expanded`, or keyboard handlers.
- **GET search:** use `<search>`, `<form method="get" action="/inventory">`,
  an associated label, and `<input class="syn-input" type="search" name="q">`.
  Native form navigation works with scripts disabled. Your server must filter
  results, preserve the query, escape untrusted input, and return a useful
  response; Syntyr does not implement a search endpoint.
- **Confirmation dialog:** use a `commandfor` + `command="show-modal"`
  button, `<dialog class="syn-dialog" aria-labelledby="...">`, and a
  `<form method="dialog">` with Cancel/Confirm choices. `method="dialog"`
  **only closes the dialog**; it does not submit a destructive action or
  authorize a mutation. A real save/delete must use a secure application
  endpoint or separately tested application logic. Provide a reachable
  non-dialog fallback for older browsers without invoker commands.
- **Datalist suggestions:** connect a labeled text input's `list` to a
  native `<datalist id="...">`. Users can enter text not in the suggestions.
  For restricted values use native `<select>` with optional `<optgroup>`;
  do not claim `datalist` is an accessible custom combobox.
- **Meter and output:** use `<meter min max low high optimum value>` for a
  bounded measurement and `<output>` for a computed or server-provided
  result. Provide readable labels and numeric text. Values do not update
  automatically: the server or application must calculate and synchronize
  them when inputs change.

[Open the script-free native interaction demo](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/native-interactions.html)
or [copy each recipe from the component catalog](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/catalog.html).
The page is intentionally static: search reloads with a query string,
dialog confirmation has no side effects, and output is a snapshot. In a
production application, implement real search and mutations in the host.

These patterns compose existing `syn-form`, `syn-input`, `syn-details`,
`syn-dialog`, `syn-inline`, and native HTML; adding a separate
`.syn-accordion`, `.syn-search`, or `.syn-confirm` class would duplicate
styles, selectors, documentation, and long-term compatibility obligations.
Native picker popup details and suggestion menus vary among browsers.
Test keyboard interaction, forced colors, zoom/reflow, and real product
copy in the target browsers. **Application-owned behavior** includes
search filtering, validation on the server, destructive action
authorization, and live calculations; none are provided by CSS.

## Native horizontal carousels

The existing opt-in `syntyr.media.css` module supplies
`syn-media-rail--controls` for browser-generated previous/next buttons and
`syn-media-rail--markers` for optional position markers. The underlying
`syn-media-rail` continues to scroll and snap without those features.
Every marked direct child must provide a localized `data-syn-scroll-label`
for its accessible marker name.

[Copy the script-free example](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/media-entertainment.html) and read
[compatibility details and the full recipe](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/media-entertainment.md).
Do not replace real ARIA tab widgets with CSS markers, or claim that markers
provide autoplay, filtering, infinite looping or application state.

## Resource outline (nested native navigation)

A **Resource outline** is a CSS-only, progressively enhanced way to browse
hierarchical folders, account groups and assets. Load `syntyr.core.css` and
the optional `syntyr.native-recipes.css`; put `.syn-resource-outline`
on a labeled `<nav>` within `.syn-root`. Use nested unordered lists,
native disclosure via `<details><summary>` for expandable groups, and real
links for destinations. Mark exactly the current destination with
`aria-current="page"`. Use `open` on parent details when the current
record is nested inside them. Lists remain navigable when JavaScript is off.

This is **not an ARIA tree** widget: it deliberately avoids `role="tree"`,
roving tabindex, arrow-key claims or JS-managed selection. The browser
provides native disclosure keyboard semantics (Tab, Enter/Space).
A full WAI-ARIA treeview requires additional headless interaction logic
and real assistive-technology testing; it does not belong in CSS.
For moving resources, permissions, lazy loading, remote filtering, and drag
and drop, the **application** must implement authorized behavior. No CSS
state alone conveys permission to move an item.

See [the script-free resource outline example](../examples/resource-outline.html).
The nesting uses logical inline spacing to work in both LTR and RTL;
after three visual indentation levels it stops adding horizontal offset so
very deep folders remain readable at narrow widths and 400% zoom; semantic
list hierarchy and native disclosures remain intact. Long names wrap rather
than being silently truncated. Keep the
selected location visible, ensure all links have real destinations,
and test browser focus, high zoom, and forced colors in the host app.

## Individually importable CSS

Use the following **source-tree alpha.5 candidate** entrypoints after this PR
is merged and released; they are not available in the published alpha.4 package:

~~~css
@import "@syntyr/css/components/tokens.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/base.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/buttons.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/forms.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/form-composition.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/components/overlays.css";
@import "@syntyr/css/native-recipes.css";
~~~

Every component CSS file is directly generated from its original source, using
the same order and cascade layers as core. Tokens, then base, then components,
then optional recipes is the supported loading order. Form-composition requires
forms. Do **not** load core and component entrypoints together, or styles will be
duplicated. Runtime CSS dependencies, imports and JavaScript are not included in
these distributables. In plain HTML, link the equivalent checked-in files under
the dist directory. Use version-pinned self-hosted assets in production.

If no selective loading is needed, use core plus the optional recipe sheet:

~~~html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.native-recipes.css">
~~~

## Native anchored popovers and modal commands

~~~html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="actions">Actions</button>
<div id="actions" popover class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored">
  <a href="/settings">Settings</a>
</div>
<button type="button" class="syn-button" commandfor="report" command="show-modal">Report</button>
<dialog id="report" class="syn-dialog" aria-labelledby="report-title">
  <h2 id="report-title">Report</h2>
  <form method="dialog"><button type="submit">Close</button></form>
</dialog>
~~~

Native popover invokers provide an implicit CSS anchor in supporting browsers.
The anchored variant uses position-area plus block/inline flip candidates; in
other browsers it falls back to Syntyr's existing fixed corner positioning.
For vital actions, links remain real links. Modal invoker commands are not
universally available in older browsers, so provide a navigable fallback for
critical content or use a small explicit progressive enhancement in the host.
Transitions do **not** ship in core. To opt into native popover/dialog
motion, load the additional `syntyr.motion.css` file, then add
`.syn-popover--transition` to a `.syn-popover` or
`.syn-dialog--transition` to a `.syn-dialog`. Both class and file are
required. The motion module honors reduced-motion preferences; without
either opt-in, dialogs and popovers use their native static behavior.
The native recipe gallery pairs its dialog command with a `<details>`
disclosure exposing equivalent critical information on older engines.
Native browsers own focus management, Escape and dialog inertness; the stylesheet
does not implement a custom ARIA menu.

## Native direction-aware presentation

The core popover's fixed-corner fallback and optional cut-corner panels use
CSS **logical** inset properties. They follow the document's text direction
(LTR or **RTL**) without a new theme or variant. Anchored popovers use the
browser's native block/inline positioning and flip candidates when available.
Optional activity timelines also place their markers on inline-start. Native
`dir="rtl"` controls direction; components keep semantic document order.

## Floating labels

~~~html
<div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
  <input id="name" name="name" class="syn-input" placeholder=" " required>
  <label for="name" class="syn-floating-label">Full name</label>
</div>
~~~

Both floating and stacked labels remain real pointer targets; clicking a label
focuses its associated native control without JavaScript.

Keep a persistent programmatic label with for/id. The one-space placeholder
is a deliberate :placeholder-shown state hook, **not** the accessible label.

The field becomes a **stacked, wrapping label above the input** when its own
container is narrow (21rem or less). This protects visible field identification
when users enlarge text, including long translated labels. At wider sizes the
floating presentation remains. In RTL documents (`dir="rtl"`), the floating
label shrinks toward the right-hand inline-start edge rather than drifting
left. The label is always a real `<label for>`; the CSS never substitutes
placeholders for an accessible name. Test real browser zoom and translations
in consuming applications.

Use only for text-like controls that implement placeholder-shown. Avoid for
date, color, select, checkbox, radio and unsupported types. Validate contrast
and long translated labels in the actual application.

### Label-first floating fields

Use the same native label and input in either source order:

~~~html
<div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
  <label class="syn-floating-label" for="company">Company</label>
  <input class="syn-input" id="company" name="company" placeholder=" " autocomplete="organization">
</div>
~~~

Modern browsers use :has() to float label-first markup when the input is
focused or filled. Input-first markup remains the fallback for older engines.
Keep a real for/id association; placeholder text is not an accessible label.
At narrow container widths, both orders become a traditional stacked field.

### Native file feedback and search controls

Plain file inputs in .syn-semantic preserve their native file picker.
For aria-invalid="true", Syntyr adds a visible error border to the file
input even when the user-agent default has no border. Use a real explanation
associated with aria-describedby; CSS does not perform validation or upload.
The native search clear affordance is preserved with inline-end padding
in both explicit .syn-input and scoped classless modes.

~~~html
<div class="syn-semantic">
  <label for="proof">Proof-of-posting photo</label>
  <input type="file" id="proof" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="proof-error">
  <small id="proof-error" class="syn-error">Upload a photo to continue.</small>
</div>
~~~

## Semantic timelines and captioned code

~~~html
<ol class="syn-timeline" role="list">
  <li><time datetime="2026-11-15">15 November</time>Published</li>
</ol>

<figure class="syn-code-figure">
  <figcaption id="example-caption">example.go</figcaption>
  <pre tabindex="0" aria-labelledby="example-caption"><code>package main</code></pre>
</figure>
~~~

An ordered list communicates sequence; date/time labels are optional.
The figure gives code an authentic, accessible caption, and the focusable pre
supports keyboard scrolling of wide code samples.

## Server-rendering and framework use

- **Go templates and templ:** Emit the same native HTML; escape dynamic label,
  body and code text with the renderer and ensure stable unique id/for pairs.
- **Rust Askama:** Render this markup in a regular Askama template. Escape
  dynamic content; let forms submit to real routes.
- **Astro:** Import selected CSS files through its CSS pipeline, render standard
  HTML, and use Astro islands only for behaviors that require application state.
- **HTMX:** Keep popovertarget and commandfor on native controls; for actions
  that mutate data, use real forms/links and HTMX only as progressive enhancement.

### Go html/template

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email"
           type="email" value="{{ .Email }}" placeholder=" " required>
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

The standard Go html/template engine escapes the Email value by context.

### Rust Askama

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email"
           type="email" value="{{ email }}" placeholder=" " required>
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

Use Askama's HTML autoescaping, unique IDs when rendering multiple forms, and
normal server-side validation.

### Astro

~~~astro
---
import "@syntyr/css/components/tokens.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/base.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/buttons.css";
import "@syntyr/css/components/forms.css";
import "@syntyr/css/native-recipes.css";
---
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post">
  <div class="syn-root syn-field syn-field--floating">
    <input class="syn-input" id="astro-email" name="email"
           type="email" placeholder=" " required />
    <label class="syn-floating-label" for="astro-email">Email address</label>
  </div>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
~~~

In a real Astro page place the syn-root scope around the entire page region,
as in this form. Package imports
are source candidate features until a corresponding npm release is published.

### HTMX (optional enhancement)

~~~html
<form class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio" action="/profile" method="post"
      hx-post="/profile" hx-target="#profile-result" hx-swap="outerHTML">
  <label for="profile-email">Email address</label>
  <input class="syn-input" id="profile-email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
<p id="profile-result" role="status" aria-live="polite"></p>
~~~

The action/method pair remains functional without HTMX. Host applications must
provide their own HTMX script and server response semantics.

This guide intentionally avoids wrappers and framework-specific JavaScript.
Refer to [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md) and the
[progressive enhancement guide (online)](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/progressive-enhancement.md) for host behavior
and fallbacks.

---

## Source: docs/semantic-components.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/semantic-components.md

# Semantic HTML component recipes

Build article previews, breadcrumbs, citations, metadata lists, change histories,
internationalized labels, tables, FAQs, search forms, measured status, and
responsive media with **native HTML**. Syntyr styles
these elements without replacing browser semantics or adding a JavaScript runtime.
These are copy-owned markup compositions in the free MIT core—not new JS widgets.

[View the live semantic component gallery](../examples/semantic-compositions.html).
For the existing forms, dialogs, search and disclosure patterns, see
[native platform patterns](native-patterns.md).

## Install semantic styling

Load core first, semantic second. Both are plain CSS; styles apply only to a
`.syn-root.syn-semantic` element or a `.syn-semantic` subtree inside
`.syn-root`. Classless elements are styled automatically. Add
`data-syn-semantic` to classed elements **only** when opting them into the
semantic rules. A classed element keeps its explicitly chosen component styles.

~~~html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/dist/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/dist/syntyr.semantic.css">
<main class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article><h1>Semantic HTML, styled by Syntyr</h1></article>
</main>
~~~

Use version-pinned stylesheets from your own deployment in production. These
examples require **no JavaScript**. Any data lookup, routing, persistence or
change handling still belongs to the server or host application.

## Article preview with publication date

Use `article` for a self-contained work and `time[datetime]` for
machine-readable dates. Avoid `article` merely to get a bordered card:
use `.syn-panel` on an ordinary container instead.

~~~html
<article>
  <header>
    <h2><a href="/notes/semantic-html">Semantic HTML in practice</a></h2>
    <p>Published <time datetime="2026-11-16">16 November 2026</time></p>
  </header>
  <p>A compact guide to meaningful browser-native markup.</p>
  <footer><small>Documentation team</small></footer>
</article>
~~~

## Breadcrumb navigation

Use a real `nav` landmark, an ordered list and `aria-current="page"`.
Syntyr already provides `.syn-breadcrumbs`; do not create a second breadcrumb
component or hand-code presentational separator characters.

~~~html
<nav class="syn-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/docs">Docs</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">Semantics</li>
  </ol>
</nav>
~~~

## Definitions and structured metadata

Use `dl`, `dt`, and `dd` for name/value pairs; `data[value]` for a
machine-readable value, `abbr[title]` for a genuine abbreviation, and
`time[datetime]` for dates. Do not use `dl` merely as a two-column grid.

~~~html
<dl>
  <dt>Plan</dt><dd>Team</dd>
  <dt>Seats</dt><dd><data value="12">12 active seats</data></dd>
  <dt>Renewal</dt><dd><time datetime="2027-01-01">1 January 2027</time></dd>
  <dt>Availability</dt><dd><abbr title="Service-level agreement">SLA</abbr> 99.9%</dd>
</dl>
~~~

## Quotation and source attribution

Use `blockquote` for a long quotation and a `figure` with
`figcaption` for its attribution. `cite` names the *work*, not its author;
do not manufacture a URL for the `blockquote[cite]` attribute.

~~~html
<figure>
  <blockquote><p>Use the language of the platform before adding an abstraction.</p></blockquote>
  <figcaption>From <cite>Semantic Design Notes</cite></figcaption>
</figure>
~~~

A `blockquote` may alternatively include a `footer` for supporting
attribution text. The optional semantic stylesheet styles that footer, without
changing the surrounding `footer` elements elsewhere on the page.

## Document revisions

The `ins` and `del` elements communicate additions and removals. Include a
valid `datetime` if the modification date is known. For live collaborative
editing or audit history, the server remains authoritative.

~~~html
<p>Retention: <del datetime="2026-11-15">90 days</del>
  <ins datetime="2026-11-16">120 days</ins>.</p>
~~~

## Multilingual pronunciation and bidi isolation

Use `ruby` and `rt` for pronunciation annotations; `rp` supplies text
fallback in browsers without ruby presentation. Syntyr deliberately does not restyle the
annotation; the browser owns ruby positioning, text size, and fallback. Use `bdi` for a
user-supplied string with unknown direction; `bdo` intentionally overrides
direction and should be used only when that behavior is required.

~~~html
<p>Character: <ruby>漢<rp>(</rp><rt>hàn</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby></p>
<p>Author: <bdi>مريم</bdi> — saved successfully.</p>
<p>Deliberate reverse sequence: <bdo dir="rtl">ABC</bdo></p>
~~~

## Tabular totals with a real footer

Keep a caption, column headers with `scope="col"`, row headers with
`scope="row"`, and a `tfoot` summary. The browser owns table semantics;
Syntyr's optional `tfoot` styling adds only a separator and weight. For
complex tables, connect headers using `id` and `headers` as needed.

~~~html
<table>
  <caption>Monthly license usage</caption>
  <thead><tr><th scope="col">License</th><th scope="col">Seats</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">Team</th><td>12</td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">Guest</th><td>3</td></tr>
  </tbody>
  <tfoot><tr><th scope="row">Total</th><td>15</td></tr></tfoot>
</table>
~~~

## Complementary content

A contextual `aside` is a complementary landmark, not a generic card. Apply
the existing `.syn-panel` class when a visual callout is desirable.

~~~html
<aside class="syn-panel" aria-labelledby="help-title">
  <h2 id="help-title">Implementation guidance</h2>
  <p>Keep routing, translations, and data validation in the host application.</p>
</aside>
~~~

## In-page navigation

A `nav` landmark with an accessible name and a real ordered list doubles as
an in-page table of contents. Anchor destinations must exist. Do not substitute
a fake tab interface or JavaScript scrolling for ordinary document navigation.

~~~html
<nav aria-label="On this page">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#offer">Current offer</a></li>
    <li><a href="#notes">Reference notes</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
<section id="offer" aria-labelledby="offer-heading">
  <h2 id="offer-heading">Current offer</h2>
  <p>Native content, no client-side routing required.</p>
</section>
<section id="notes" aria-labelledby="notes-heading">
  <h2 id="notes-heading">Reference notes</h2>
  <p>Each anchor points to a real heading section.</p>
</section>
~~~

## Previous price versus revision

Use `s` for content that is no longer accurate or relevant, such as a
superseded advertised price; `del` and `ins` instead describe **actual
document edits**. Use `data[value]` when the application needs a
machine-readable number, not to indicate currency on its own. Provide the
currency and billing period in visible text. Price, stock and promotion
eligibility must still be verified by the server before any transaction.

~~~html
<article>
  <h2>Team plan (example only)</h2>
  <p>Example price:
    <s><data value="39">US$39 per month</data></s>
    <strong><data value="29">US$29 per month</data></strong>
  </p>
  <p><small>Illustrative pricing, not a live Syntyr offer.</small></p>
</article>
~~~

Syntyr's optional semantic layer lightly de-emphasizes `s` but keeps its
native strikethrough. This rule remains scoped to classless or explicitly
opted-in elements inside `.syn-semantic`.

## Footnotes and return links

Use a normal `sup` with an anchor to a numbered `ol`, then include a
return link to the reference. This approach works with keyboard navigation,
screen readers, server-rendered HTML and no custom event handlers. Do not
put footnote bodies in an inaccessible hover-only tooltip.

~~~html
<p>Native links are keyboard accessible
  <sup id="note-ref-1"><a href="#note-1" aria-label="Footnote 1">1</a></sup>.
</p>
<section aria-labelledby="footnotes-title">
  <h2 id="footnotes-title">Notes</h2>
  <ol>
    <li id="note-1">A normal anchor connects the note and reference.
      <a href="#note-ref-1">Return to reference 1</a>
    </li>
  </ol>
</section>
~~~

Both IDs must be unique to the page, and links must resolve when fragments
are loaded directly. Keep the note text in the document, not generated solely
with CSS `content`.

## Technical notation and long identifiers

Prefer the HTML elements that convey meaning: `var` names a variable,
`samp` names program output, `kbd` represents keyboard input,
`sub` and `sup` retain native baseline notation, and `wbr` allows
line breaks within long identifiers. Syntyr deliberately leaves `sub`,
`sup` and `wbr` layout to the browser.

~~~html
<p>Area = <var>width</var> × <var>height</var>.
  Water is H<sub>2</sub>O; the formula is E = mc<sup>2</sup>.
</p>
<p>Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The program prints <samp>Ready</samp>.</p>
<p>Example endpoint: <code>api.example.test/<wbr>v1/<wbr>document-exports</code></p>
~~~

The domain and endpoint above are placeholders only, not production services.

## Grouped table headings

Use `colgroup` with a real `th scope="colgroup"` and subcolumn headings.
For simple tables, use `scope="col"` and `scope="row"` instead. Syntyr
already provides native cell borders and table captions; the optional
semantic styling adds a subtle `thead` background and preserves
high-contrast borders. It does not replace table accessibility semantics.

~~~html
<table>
  <caption>Example monthly accounts</caption>
  <colgroup><col></colgroup>
  <colgroup span="2"></colgroup>
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col" rowspan="2">Plan</th>
        <th scope="colgroup" colspan="2">Accounts</th></tr>
    <tr><th scope="col">Paid</th><th scope="col">Trial</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">Starter</th><td>8</td><td>3</td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">Growth</th><td>4</td><td>2</td></tr>
  </tbody>
  <tfoot><tr><th scope="row">Total</th><td>12</td><td>5</td></tr></tfoot>
</table>
~~~

## Contact details

An `address` identifies contact information for a document or its nearest
`article` context; it is **not** a generic container for any street
address. Use a genuine support link or known contact method rather than an
invented email address. The example below uses the project's actual issue
tracker.

~~~html
<footer>
  <address>Questions about this guide?
    <a href="https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/issues">
      Contact the Syntyr maintainers through Issues
    </a>.
  </address>
</footer>
~~~

## Native FAQ disclosure

Use a `details` element and its **first child** `summary` for
disclosures. Give related items the same `name` for a browser-native
single-open accordion. A single group member may start with `open`; browsers
close its peers when another member opens. This is an interaction, not a
tablist, so do not add `role="tab"` or extra JavaScript. Keep answers present
in the document for users and search engines. The optional stylesheet
distinguishes an opened panel with a soft border.

~~~html
<section aria-labelledby="faq-heading">
  <h2 id="faq-heading">FAQ</h2>
  <details name="syn-semantic-faq" open>
    <summary>Does this need JavaScript?</summary>
    <p>No. The browser handles open and closed state and keyboard use.</p>
  </details>
  <details name="syn-semantic-faq">
    <summary>Can I use it in a server-rendered app?</summary>
    <p>Yes. Keep the markup on the page and the group name unique.</p>
  </details>
</section>
~~~

For content that should be visible simultaneously, omit the shared `name`.
Do not hide legal, essential or time-critical information behind an unannounced
disclosure.

## Semantic issue search

Use `search` for the page's search landmark and a native GET form, with a
visible label and an actual endpoint. This example searches the public Syntyr
GitHub issue tracker; it works without client-side JavaScript, although
submitting navigates away to GitHub.

~~~html
<search>
  <form action="https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/issues" method="get">
    <label for="issues-query">Search Syntyr issues</label>
    <input id="issues-query" type="search" name="q" required
           placeholder="Example: accessibility">
    <button type="submit">Find issues</button>
  </form>
</search>
~~~

The host application is responsible for providing a real backend for any
site-local search. Do not present a demo-only search box as functional.

## Grouped choice form

Use `fieldset` and `legend` for the shared form prompt, `label` for
control identification, and `optgroup` to group related `option`
elements. Native select popup appearance is browser-owned. Here the chosen
topic is sent as a GET query to the real public issue tracker.

~~~html
<form action="https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/issues" method="get">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Browse a topic</legend>
    <label for="issue-topic">Issue topic</label>
    <select name="q" id="issue-topic" required>
      <option value="">Choose a topic</option>
      <optgroup label="HTML">
        <option value="semantic">Semantic HTML</option>
        <option value="accessibility">Accessibility</option>
      </optgroup>
      <optgroup label="Styles">
        <option value="css">CSS</option>
        <option value="themes">Themes</option>
      </optgroup>
    </select>
    <button type="submit">View matching issues</button>
  </fieldset>
</form>
~~~

Do not replace `fieldset` with a visually similar generic container where
controls genuinely share a question.

## Progress and measurement

Use `progress[value][max]` for progress **toward completion**. Use
`meter[value][min][max]` for a bounded measurement such as utilization or a
rating. The `low`, `high` and `optimum` attributes describe value
quality, not completion progress. Include an actual `label` (or equivalent
accessible name) and visible readable value. `output` can display a
server-computed result; it does **not** recalculate automatically in response
to changing inputs without host logic.

~~~html
<section aria-labelledby="status-heading">
  <h2 id="status-heading">Illustrative status</h2>
  <label for="review-progress">Review progress: 7 of 10 complete</label>
  <progress id="review-progress" value="7" max="10">7 of 10</progress>
  <label for="capacity-meter">Sample capacity: 68%</label>
  <meter id="capacity-meter" value="68" min="0" max="100"
         low="30" high="85" optimum="70">68%</meter>
  <p>Calculated review total:
    <output name="review-total">7 completed reviews</output>
  </p>
</section>
~~~

All figures in this example are illustrative rather than live metrics.
For indeterminate progress, omit `value` and provide an accompanying
status message.

## Responsive captioned media

Use `picture` and `source[media][srcset]` for browser-driven responsive
art direction, `img` with meaningful alternative text and intrinsic
dimensions to prevent layout shifts, and `figure` with `figcaption` when a
caption belongs to the media. This example switches between two actual
Syntyr Studio screenshots at narrow widths. There is no carousel or script.

~~~html
<figure>
  <picture>
    <source media="(max-width: 600px)"
            srcset="../docs/previews/studio-settings.webp">
    <img src="../docs/previews/studio-editor.webp"
         width="1120" height="700" loading="lazy" decoding="async"
         alt="Syntyr Studio interface: settings on small screens and editor on larger screens">
  </picture>
  <figcaption>Two Syntyr Studio views, selected by viewport width.</figcaption>
</figure>
~~~

Supply valid paths relative to the **published page**, not the Markdown
document location. These paths assume the snippet runs in the examples
directory as in the live component gallery. If there is no meaningful
art-direction change, prefer a single responsive `img` instead.

## Native suggestions with datalist

Use `input[list]` with an associated `datalist` when you want to
**suggest** common text entries without restricting what the user can type.
Unlike `select`, it does not create an exhaustive set of choices. The
`input` still needs a visible `label`, a real `name` for submission, and
server-side validation. The browser owns how suggestions appear; do not try
to skin a datalist popup.

This working example submits a GET query to Syntyr's public issue tracker.

~~~html
<form action="https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/issues" method="get">
  <label for="topic-suggest">Search issues (try a suggested topic)</label>
  <input id="topic-suggest" name="q" type="search"
         list="reference-topic-suggestions" required
         placeholder="Type a topic">
  <datalist id="reference-topic-suggestions">
    <option value="semantic"></option>
    <option value="accessibility"></option>
    <option value="themes"></option>
    <option value="typography"></option>
  </datalist>
  <button type="submit">Search issues on GitHub</button>
</form>
~~~

**No JavaScript is required** for suggestions. Use `select` instead when
the submitted value must come from a finite set.

## Glossary and abbreviations

Use a real definition list for a collection of terms and their definitions.
`dfn` identifies the term being defined, and `abbr[title]` expands an
abbreviation the first time it matters. Do not use `dfn` as a decorative
italic treatment or `dl` as an arbitrary two-column layout.

~~~html
<section aria-labelledby="glossary-heading">
  <h2 id="glossary-heading">Glossary</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt><dfn>Native semantics</dfn></dt>
    <dd>Meaning provided by HTML elements without custom roles.</dd>
    <dt><dfn>ARIA</dfn></dt>
    <dd><abbr title="Accessible Rich Internet Applications">ARIA</abbr>
        extends accessibility semantics only where native HTML is insufficient.</dd>
  </dl>
</section>
~~~

## Highlighted excerpts and quotations

`mark` indicates a relevant excerpt in its current context, such as a
search match, while `q` denotes an inline quotation. The `cite` element
names the cited **work**, rather than the author or a source URL. Do not
manually insert quote-mark characters around `q` when the browser already
provides them. Syntyr already styles `mark`, `q`, and `cite`; no extra
components or runtime are necessary.

~~~html
<article aria-labelledby="excerpt-heading">
  <h2 id="excerpt-heading">Highlighted documentation excerpt</h2>
  <p><mark>Native HTML</mark> allows browser-owned focus and semantics.</p>
  <p><q>Syntyr styles these elements without replacing browser semantics</q>
     — <cite><a href="../docs/semantic-components.html">
       Semantic HTML component recipes</a></cite>.</p>
</article>
~~~

The quoted line comes from this guide's introduction. For search results,
the server supplies the real match and safely escaped text; never inject
untrusted HTML into highlighted excerpts.

## Chronological ordered list

Use `ol` for genuinely ordered events and `time[datetime]` for dates
that machines can parse. `reversed` and `start` preserve native
numbering for newest-first sequences; they are not substitutes for sorting
the data server-side. This checklist is illustrative, **not** an actual
Syntyr release history.

~~~html
<section aria-labelledby="history-heading">
  <h2 id="history-heading">Illustrative release steps</h2>
  <ol reversed start="3">
    <li><time datetime="2026-11-16">16 November 2026</time>: Publish examples</li>
    <li><time datetime="2026-11-15">15 November 2026</time>: Validate HTML</li>
    <li><time datetime="2026-11-14">14 November 2026</time>: Draft content</li>
  </ol>
</section>
~~~

Use normal `ol` without `reversed` for a conventional chronological
timeline or instructions progressing from step one.

## Mathematical notation with MathML

Native **MathML** gives equations structural meaning: `math`, `mrow`,
`mi`, `mn`, `mo`, and `msup` identify the formula and its parts.
Include readable explanatory text in a `figcaption`; avoid images of
math without meaningful text alternatives. Annotation may preserve
source notation for compatible tools, but browsers own layout.

~~~html
<figure>
  <math display="block">
    <semantics>
      <mrow>
        <msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
        <mo>+</mo>
        <msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
        <mo>=</mo>
        <msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup>
      </mrow>
      <annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a^2 + b^2 = c^2</annotation>
    </semantics>
  </math>
  <figcaption>Example Pythagorean identity: a squared plus b squared equals c squared.</figcaption>
</figure>
~~~

MathML is browser-native, **not styled by the optional semantic sheet**.
Test presentation and accessibility with the actual browsers your users
need to support.

## Resource command list

A native `menu` is an unordered list of **commands/actions**, not an ARIA
application menu with arrow-key behavior. Use actual links for navigation
actions and `button` only when it performs an implemented action. Do not
add `role="menu"` unless you intend to implement its complete keyboard
interaction contract.

~~~html
<section aria-labelledby="resources-heading">
  <h2 id="resources-heading">Reference actions</h2>
  <menu>
    <li><a href="../docs/semantic-components.html">Read semantic recipes</a></li>
    <li><a href="native-elements.html">Browse native controls</a></li>
    <li><a href="https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/issues">Report an issue</a></li>
  </menu>
</section>
~~~

All destinations are real links. Ordinary `ul` remains preferable for
a list of information rather than actions.

**Accessibility and maintenance:** Keep real heading order and link destinations,
avoid adding redundant ARIA roles to native elements, test browser reflow and
right-to-left content, and do not add JavaScript just to imitate HTML controls.
`ruby`, `bdi`, `bdo`, `rp` and table navigation are browser-owned behavior.

---

## Source: docs/composition-adoption.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/composition-adoption.md

# Intrinsic layout compositions: inline clusters and sidecars

Syntyr uses scoped native CSS, not a JavaScript layout engine. These patterns
are available in the **unreleased alpha.5 source candidate** under
`dist/syntyr.core.css`. No additional JavaScript or CSS modules are required.

[Open the no-JavaScript composition demo](../examples/composition-adoption.html).

## Use syn-inline for a wrapping cluster

An existing `.syn-inline` is the cluster primitive; Syntyr does **not** add an
identical `.syn-cluster` alias. It wraps naturally and now exposes optional
`--syn-inline-align`, `--syn-inline-justify`, and `--syn-inline-gap` custom
properties.

~~~html
<nav class="syn-inline" aria-label="Contact filters"
     style="--syn-inline-justify:space-between">
  <a href="/contacts?status=active">Active</a>
  <a href="/contacts?status=inactive">Inactive</a>
  <a href="/contacts">All contacts</a>
</nav>
~~~

Use a real `nav` for navigation and a real `form` for filtering inputs.
The class changes layout only; it never implies tab semantics or keyboard
behavior. Existing `.syn-inline` layouts retain their default center
alignment and start justification.

## Use syn-sidecar for an intrinsic main + aside

A two-child `.syn-sidecar` puts the **main content first** and the supplementary
aside second in document and focus order. It wraps on available container width
without viewport breakpoints, JavaScript, or an explicit container query.
A lone child remains the main region and keeps the min-size and
unbroken-text overflow protections.

~~~html
<div class="syn-root syn-sidecar" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <main class="syn-panel">
    <h1>Campaigns</h1>
    <p>The principal content remains first in the accessibility tree.</p>
  </main>
  <aside class="syn-panel" aria-label="Campaign insights">
    <h2>Insights</h2>
    <p>Supplementary context.</p>
  </aside>
</div>
~~~

Custom properties belong on the layout container:

| Property | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--syn-sidecar-gap` | `--syn-space-3` | Space between regions |
| `--syn-sidecar-main-min` | `28rem` | Minimum preferred size of the main area before wrapping |
| `--syn-sidecar-aside-width` | `16rem` | Preferred width of the supplementary area |
| `--syn-sidecar-align` | `start` | Cross-axis alignment |

Do not add absolute positioning or hide the aside on small screens. CSS intrinsic
wrapping responds to the *actual available width*, including embedded sidebars,
rather than guessing from the viewport. Content may still overflow if
application-defined children use fixed dimensions; make tables and code blocks
scrollable and keyboard reachable where necessary.

## Import only what you need

For no-build consumers, the preferred option is one self-hosted
`syntyr.core.css` stylesheet. For selective component loading, use the
prebuilt CSS files in order: `components/tokens.css`,
`components/base.css`, then `components/layout.css` and any additional
components. Do not load core and these component files together. The
`form-composition` module also needs `forms`.

The `--syn-inline-*` and `--syn-sidecar-*` properties are public
customization points; they do not require an app-side CSS compiler.
Syntyr's optional [selective builder](selective-builds.md) can assemble
a single stylesheet without scanning templates or purging dynamic classes.

See the [Go server-rendered starter](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/tree/main/examples/go-htmx) for a
working app whose native GET route can optionally return HTMX fragments.
Application state, accessibility behavior and data authorization always
belong to the host, not to these layout classes.

For optional browser verification, run `python3 tests/composition_adoption_browser.py`
from a checkout with Playwright and browser engines installed. It checks
wide, narrow, and embedded widths; WebKit needs its native system dependencies.
The release CSS and the example itself do not require Playwright.

---

## Source: docs/radix-integration.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/radix-integration.md

# Optional Radix Primitives visual adapter

Syntyr core remains plain CSS with zero runtime JavaScript and zero React dependencies. Radix is a **separate application choice**. Its components own the accessible name, **ARIA** attributes, focus management, keyboard controls and state updates. Syntyr only adds styling.

## Install and opt in

In a React project using Radix Primitives, add a link **after** the core CSS:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/radix/states.css">
```

Copy [the adapter](../integrations/radix/states.css) into your project, or reference its repository source. Do not load it when you do not use Radix. It is **not** included in `syntyr.all.css`, either.

Wrap the relevant app area in `.syn-root`. Apply `.syn-radix` on that root, on a container inside it, **or directly on a stateful Syntyr control** to opt in only that control. If Radix portals content to the document body, set that portal's `container` inside the styled root, or style the portal explicitly. Do not assume portal content inherits Syntyr tokens when it is mounted outside the root.

## Example: controlled behavior, CSS presentation

```jsx
import * as Accordion from "@radix-ui/react-accordion";
import * as Toggle from "@radix-ui/react-toggle";

export function Controls() {
  return (
    <section className="syn-root syn-radix" data-syn-theme="studio">
      <Toggle.Root className="syn-button" aria-label="Pin dashboard">
        Pin dashboard
      </Toggle.Root>
      <Accordion.Root type="single" collapsible>
        <Accordion.Item value="filters">
          <Accordion.Header>
            <Accordion.Trigger className="syn-button syn-accordion-trigger">
              Advanced filters
            </Accordion.Trigger>
          </Accordion.Header>
          <Accordion.Content className="syn-accordion-content">
            <p>Additional filters belong here.</p>
          </Accordion.Content>
        </Accordion.Item>
      </Accordion.Root>
    </section>
  );
}
```

Radix supplies `data-state="on"`, `data-state="open"`, `data-state="closed"`, and `data-disabled` where applicable. The adapter consumes only those documented state hooks on **explicit Syntyr component classes**. It does not create a generic `data-state` styling API, and it does not replace Radix behavior.

## Accessibility and compatibility boundaries

- Test with keyboard only (Enter, Space, Arrow keys where appropriate, Escape) and screen readers; CSS passing a contract test is **not** an accessibility certification.
- Use a native button or Radix trigger for actions. Visual `[data-disabled]` states do not prevent click handlers from running; Radix/application logic must enforce disabled behavior.
- Preserve the focus-visible indication from Syntyr core and verify contrasts for all themes and custom token overrides.
- Avoid CSS-only emulations of focus traps, listbox navigation, complex comboboxes or dialogs.
- The adapter does not guarantee complete styling for every Radix primitive. Extend it with component-specific classes only when real use cases justify maintenance.

Related: [copy-owned component recipes](component-recipes.md), [framework integrations](framework-integrations.md).

---

## Source: docs/distribution.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/distribution.md

# Syntyr CSS distribution

Syntyr CSS is MIT-licensed. No NPM install, JavaScript runtime, fonts,
icons, Sass compiler or CSS framework is required to use the distributed CSS.

## Recommended: self-host a versioned stylesheet

1. Download the asset from the [GitHub release](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.4), or copy the matching file from the tag.
2. Put `syntyr.core.css` in your application's static CSS directory.
3. Load it normally:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Initialize</button>
</section>
```

The stylesheet's path is *your* path; mount or copy the file there.
The above works with Go templates, plain HTML, Astro, HTMX, React and other
renderers. See [the framework integration guide](framework-integrations.md) for
HTMX request-state classes, optional semantic markers, and server-side fragments. Add `syn-page` to the root only if you want full-page min-height.

## Embed inside an existing CMS theme (unreleased alpha.5)

The alpha.5 source builds a separate `dist/syntyr.embed.css` entrypoint
from the canonical core CSS, removing its outer CSS cascade layers to avoid
the normal layered-versus-unlayered theme-precedence trap. Load it **instead
of** `syntyr.core.css` for self-hosted Syntyr sections on WordPress, Shopify,
Webflow or similar themes. This file is not in published alpha.4 releases;
the CSS still uses the same `.syn-root` namespace and no runtime JavaScript.
See the [site-builder integration guide](site-builders.md) for platform limits
and copyable snippets.

## Offline SaaS preview in the next release ZIP (unreleased alpha.5)

The alpha.5 source candidate now packages `examples/saas.html` together with
`dist/syntyr.core.css` and `dist/syntyr.recipes.css`. After building or
extracting the **alpha.5** ZIP, open `examples/saas.html` directly in your
browser. Its relative stylesheets resolve within the extracted archive, so it
requires **no internet connection, local server, npm, build step or runtime
JavaScript**. You can edit the HTML and CSS locally to test integration.

This is a static **illustrative SaaS dashboard**: fictional metrics, no real
account data, authentication, filtering, API calls, or backend actions. To use
it in an application, replace sample values with server-rendered data and wire
navigation and mutations to your own server. The already published **alpha.4**
release does *not* contain this packaged example; the next alpha.5 release
has not been published yet.

## Command launcher ZIP example (unreleased alpha.5)

The optional command launcher example points to three standalone HTML
examples included in the release ZIP: the preset preview, native resource
outline, and SaaS dashboard. Both the script-free navigation and enhanced
native-dialog links resolve without fetching any unbundled docs assets.

For the interactive Ctrl/Command+K module, serve the extracted alpha.5
release directory over local HTTP, as explained for the resizable workspace
above. From the extracted ZIP's top-level folder, run:

    python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/examples/command-launcher.html.
The native navigation stays usable without JavaScript on a file:// URL, but
the optional module may be blocked by browser file-origin restrictions.
No server is necessary for the static examples/saas.html preview.

## One-file semantic starter (unreleased alpha.5 source)

For a Pico-like HTML workflow, `dist/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` combines core and semantic CSS into a single file. Copy it to your static assets, then opt in on the region you want styled:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic-bundle.css">
<body class="syn-root syn-page syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <main class="syn-shell">
    <article><h1>Dashboard</h1><button type="button">Open</button></article>
  </main>
</body>
```

Only the controls and elements inside `.syn-root.syn-semantic` are styled semantically. This is **not** Pico's globally classless behavior: the root scope is deliberate. No script or build tool is required. [See the runnable starter](../examples/semantic-starter.html) and the [Pico migration guide](from-pico.md). **This file is not in the published alpha.4 release** and its `/dist/` URL is not an immutable release asset; pin a released version once alpha.5 is actually published. Do not load `core.css` or `semantic.css` alongside this bundle.

## Single-file presets (experimental alpha.5 source)

Choose one self-contained file and self-host it. There are **no stylesheet
imports or runtime dependencies**. Each preset includes tokens, core components,
and scoped opt-in semantic HTML styling:

| Preset | Distribution | When to choose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal | `dist/presets/minimal.css` | Documentation, forms and simple websites |
| SaaS | `dist/presets/saas.css` | Business sites, dashboards, HTMX/server-rendered apps; explicit `syn-u-*` helpers |
| Cinematic | `dist/presets/cinematic.css` | Optional Grid/Noir effects, precision frames, native CSS motion |

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr-saas.css">
<main class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <article><h1>Settings</h1><label for="email">Email</label>
    <input type="email" id="email" required>
    <button type="button">Preview</button>
  </article>
</main>
```

Only the path is application-defined; copy `dist/presets/saas.css` to match.
**Do not stack presets** or add core/semantic/recipes CSS already inside a
preset. Styles are still isolated to `.syn-root`, while bare element styling
requires `.syn-semantic`. Native dialogs/popovers/forms retain browser behavior;
Syntyr adds no component runtime. `data-syn-theme` and `--syn-*` custom
properties remain the theme API in every preset.

Advanced users can keep a single CSS output but omit unused core components
with the optional, stdlib-only `scripts/build_selective.py --components ...
--modules ... --output ...` build. That optimization is not a consumer
requirement and does **not** purge dynamic selectors or minify CSS.

`metadata/css-contract.v1.json` is a machine-readable, deterministic
**distribution artifact manifest**: it declares preset source order, file
names, raw/gzip bytes and SHA-256 hashes, together with the library version.
The `v1` suffix versions the **manifest schema**, not the public CSS API,
which remains experimental until an explicit v1 release. `build.py --check`
rejects stale CSS and contract manifests. See [CSS API stability](api-stability.md)
and [optional visual regression testing](visual-regression.md).

Try the [script-free preset demonstration](../examples/preset-preview.html).
This is present in the alpha.5 source candidate, **not published alpha.4**.

## Optional npm/package-manager distribution

A CSS-only `@syntyr/css` manifest is available in the alpha.5 repository candidate, but **it has not been published to npm**. See [package-manager installation and local tarball testing](package-managers.md) for supported imports and an explicit no-publication boundary. No package manager is required for the documented self-hosted stylesheet path.

## Optional native animation companion

Syntyr remains CSS-only by default. Applications that need *programmatic* motion
can separately import `dist/syntyr.animate.mjs` (native Web Animations API and
IntersectionObserver only). No script is included in core or `syntyr.all.css`.
See the [animation API guide](animation.md) and the
[runnable example](../examples/animation.html).

## Optional themes and semantic HTML

Grid, Noir and Studio ship in the **same** core stylesheet; set
`data-syn-theme="grid"` or `data-syn-theme="noir"` or `data-syn-theme="studio"` on the scoped root.
You can nest differently themed elements.

The unreleased alpha.5 candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal using the same scoped `data-syn-theme` contract. The published alpha.4 release includes Grid, Noir and Studio only.

Load `syntyr.semantic.css` after core **only** if you want automatic semantic
element styles within `.syn-semantic`. For static glows and decorative grid
effects, load `syntyr.effects.css` after core. SaaS, business and terminal layouts
are opt-in via `syntyr.recipes.css`. Optional frame geometry is in `syntyr.geometry.css`.
The alpha.5 working tree additionally provides `syntyr.utilities.css` for finite
layout helpers and `syntyr.print.css` for print-friendly reports. System-aware
Grid/Studio `data-syn-theme="auto"` is already included in core CSS, with
no additional stylesheet or runtime JavaScript. See the
[progressive-enhancement guide](progressive-enhancement.md) for examples.
The optional `syntyr.symbols.css` adds BYO-SVG icon sizing, literal Unicode styling and ASCII/box-drawing alignment without shipping fonts or icons; see [symbols and accessibility](symbols.md).

`syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` bundles core and semantic styles with scoped opt-in.
`syntyr.css` bundles core and effects. `syntyr.all.css` bundles all modules
while still requiring `.syn-semantic` to opt into semantic element styles.
Avoid loading these bundles alongside their component files: that duplicates CSS. Optional utilities live in the final `syn.utilities` cascade layer, allowing explicitly applied utility classes to override ordinary component declarations; see [the architecture policy](../ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Loading contract at a glance

| Goal | Stylesheet choice | Requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Explicit components | `syntyr.core.css` | `.syn-root` wraps the component subtree |
| Plain semantic HTML | `syntyr.semantic-bundle.css` | Add `.syn-semantic` to the scoped root |
| Some components only | `components/tokens.css`, `components/base.css`, then selected component styles | Keep order; include `forms.css` with `form-composition.css` |
| Application recipes | `syntyr.core.css` followed by `syntyr.recipes.css` | Use explicitly named recipe classes |
| All features | `syntyr.all.css` | Never combine with the constituent files |

Avoid combining bundles with their constituent CSS. Each separately imported
component file intentionally has **no runtime `@import`**; load tokens and base
first. Use the [intrinsic composition guide](composition-adoption.md) to build
dashboard layouts without JavaScript or viewport-specific hacks.

## Optional explicit selective build

Applications needing fewer core components can assemble a custom CSS file with
the Python standard-library-only `scripts/build_selective.py`. It does not scan
templates or purge individual selectors, and does not alter published assets.
See [selective builds and their limits](selective-builds.md).

## Pinned CDN for prototyping

```html
<link rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/v/0.3.0-alpha.4/syntyr.core.css">
```

The first-party Cloudflare CDN serves frozen, checksum-verified CSS releases
from a global edge network. Unversioned `/dist/` URLs can change with builds;
pin `/v/<version>/` instead. The documentation's optional theme editor
has JavaScript, but the library CSS and consumer sites do not require it.
For production applications, copying the versioned CSS to your own origin
usually avoids an additional hostname connection.

## Release artifacts and guarantees

The published alpha.4 release contains seven SYNTYR CSS distributions. The
unreleased alpha.5 source candidate includes modular SYNTYR distributions,
including the optional utilities, print and symbols stylesheets, plus
the terminal ANSI palette JSON, this guide, MIT license, and README. No retired compatibility aliases are shipped. The ZIP is created deterministically using only
Python's standard library:

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/package_release.py
```

Both visual themes and all essential components are MIT-licensed. Commercial
premium templates, if introduced, will be independently authored and sold
separately. This v0.3 alpha is **not** a v1 production compatibility guarantee;
cross-browser and full accessibility audits are still release gates.

The `syn-` selectors, `--syn-` custom properties and `data-syn-` attributes are the only supported source API.
