## Source: docs/mobile-frameworks.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/mobile-frameworks.md

# Syntyr on mobile: React Native, Expo, Flutter, SwiftUI and Compose

**Status: opt-in source adapter (alpha.5 candidate), not published as a native
package.** Syntyr's web CSS does **not** execute in the native iOS or Android
renderers. The supported portable contract is **literal design tokens** from
one existing source, `src/tokens.css`. Browser-only components and behaviors
must be implemented with native controls.

| Target | Adoption route | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React Native / Expo (iOS, Android) | Copy `integrations/react-native/{tokens,styles}.ts` | Native colors, spacing, fonts, basic surface/input/button style objects |
| React Native Web / Expo Web | Same native style adapter for shared screens; Syntyr CSS in web-only HTML | Native `View` / `Text` do not become Syntyr HTML components |
| Flutter | Bundle `metadata/mobile/syntyr.tokens.json` as an asset | Theme data mapped to Flutter widgets |
| SwiftUI | Add the JSON asset to an Xcode target | Colors, spacing and metrics mapped to SwiftUI controls |
| Jetpack Compose | Add JSON to `src/main/assets/` | Colors and sizing mapped to Compose Material themes |
| Ionic / Capacitor (web-powered) | Load Syntyr's existing CSS normally | Full browser CSS support in the WebView; test platform-specific accessibility |
| NativeScript / .NET MAUI | Parse the same portable JSON | Custom native style bindings; no tested adapter shipped |

## Exact token contract

Run from the Syntyr repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/export_mobile_tokens.py
python3 scripts/export_mobile_tokens.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_mobile_adapters.py -v
```

The generated files are:

- `metadata/mobile/syntyr.tokens.json`: all seven named Syntyr palettes,
  with 13 literal SRGB color roles each, per-palette `radius`/`cut`,
  shared spacing `1–5`, font sizes `xs/sm/base`, and control height.
- `integrations/react-native/tokens.ts`: the **same values** as a standalone
  typed `as const` module, with `SyntyrMobileTheme`.
- `integrations/react-native/styles.ts`: a small, copy-owned native recipe
  that uses those generated tokens. It is not a new component library.

Unit `logical-points` means the generator converts Syntyr's literal CSS
`rem` values using the explicit **16px browser baseline** (for example,
`0.75rem -> 12`). In a native UI, treat the numbers as dp on Android,
points on iOS, or logical pixels in Flutter. This is a **design scale
mapping**, not a promise of identical physical size, font metrics or dynamic
type behavior. Native consumers must adapt to accessibility font scaling,
platform text metrics and user device settings. Colors do not automatically
follow system appearance; select the desired palette.

Only literal values are exported. Derived `color-mix()`, runtime CSS
variables, hover, grid, container queries, viewport-relative typography,
motion and browser focus semantics **are deliberately excluded**. Do not
parse `dist/syntyr.core.css` at runtime or use a WebView solely to get
Syntyr-native styling.

## React Native / Expo: copy-owned, no adapter dependency

In an Expo or bare React Native app, copy both `integrations/react-native/*.ts`
files into `src/theme/`, then use:

```tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { createSyntyrNativeStyles } from "./theme/styles";

const styles = StyleSheet.create(createSyntyrNativeStyles("studio"));

export function Example() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.panel}>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" style={styles.heading}>Account</Text>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" style={styles.button}>
        <Text style={styles.buttonLabel}>Continue</Text>
      </Pressable>
    </View>
  );
}
```

See [the interactive native screen](../examples/react-native/App.tsx) for an
email field, a stateful button and a light/dark palette switch based on
`useColorScheme()`. The example is **source to copy into an existing app**,
not a separate installable Expo project; in the app, adjust relative imports.
A separate [Expo SDK 58 development smoke fixture](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/tree/main/examples/expo-native-smoke)
is provided for reproducible native TypeScript, Jest/RNTL interaction tests,
and production Android/iOS Metro bundle exports. Run `npm ci`,
`npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run export:android`, and
`npm run export:ios` from that fixture. **Metro exports do not run on
devices or produce signed native binaries**; simulator/hardware checks are
still required. The fixture imports the canonical adapter by an ignored
build-local source copy, not a second design-system implementation.
Use the host application's safe-area provider and navigation system as usual.
The example uses real `TextInput` and `Pressable` controls with accessibility
labels; gestures, screen reader behavior, validation, keyboard handling and
focus management remain the native application's responsibility.

Do **not** import `@syntyr/css`, `syntyr.core.css` or `syn-*` classes into
Android/iOS React Native screens. An Expo Web or React Native Web route can
load Syntyr CSS in **web-only markup**, or use the token adapter for shared
native components. Syntyr does not require NativeWind, Uniwind, Tamagui or
Restyle. If your application already uses a CSS-to-native system, feed it the
token values explicitly; don't assume Syntyr selectors, pseudo-classes or
browser layout features will be compiled correctly.

## Flutter

Declare the copied JSON under `flutter/assets/syntyr.tokens.json` in
`pubspec.yaml`:

```yaml
flutter:
  assets:
    - assets/syntyr.tokens.json
```

In Dart, load once and build the palette for your widgets:

```dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/services.dart' show rootBundle;

Future<ThemeData> loadSyntyrTheme(String name) async {
  final root = jsonDecode(await rootBundle.loadString(
    'assets/syntyr.tokens.json')) as Map<String, dynamic>;
  final theme = (root['themes'] as Map<String, dynamic>)[name] as Map;
  final colors = theme['colors'] as Map;
  Color color(String role) =>
      Color(int.parse('FF${(colors[role] as String).substring(1)}', radix: 16));
  return ThemeData(
    scaffoldBackgroundColor: color('bg'),
    colorScheme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(
      seedColor: color('accent'),
      surface: color('surface'),
      onSurface: color('text'),
    ),
    cardColor: color('surface'),
  );
}
```

`ColorScheme.fromSeed` computes unspecified Material roles rather than
duplicating all Syntyr roles; map `muted`, `frame`, `danger`, and
`on-accent` explicitly for exact custom widget colors.

## SwiftUI

Bundle the JSON in the app target, parse it with `JSONSerialization` or
`Decodable`, then convert RGB hex to SwiftUI `Color`. For example:

```swift
import SwiftUI

func syntyrColor(_ hex: String) -> Color {
    let value = UInt64(hex.dropFirst(), radix: 16)!
    return Color(
        .sRGB,
        red: Double((value >> 16) & 0xff) / 255,
        green: Double((value >> 8) & 0xff) / 255,
        blue: Double(value & 0xff) / 255,
        opacity: 1
    )
}

// Given the selected palette's "colors" dictionary:
// Text("Account").foregroundStyle(syntyrColor(colors["text"]!))
```

Use semantic native accessibility roles and dynamic type; a fixed design
font size is not a substitute for the user's preferred text size.

## Android Jetpack Compose

Add the JSON to `app/src/main/assets/syntyr.tokens.json`, load it through
`context.assets.open(...)`, and read `themes[themeName].colors`.
For example, once `hex` is read from the JSON:

```kotlin
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.Color

val syntyrSurface = Color(android.graphics.Color.parseColor(hex))
```

In your Compose theme, map the named palette roles to `MaterialTheme`
`colorScheme` fields; keep user font scaling and touch-target conventions.
This is a token import route, **not** a verified Compose UI toolkit.

## Ionic / Capacitor

Ionic and Capacitor usually render HTML/CSS inside a WebView, so use the
existing `dist/syntyr.core.css` on HTML nodes within a `.syn-root`:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/syntyr.core.css">
<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary" type="button">Continue</button>
</main>
```

Ionic components may use Shadow DOM; ordinary external selectors do not
cross shadow roots. Prefer styling Syntyr-owned HTML, or the Ionic component's
documented CSS custom properties/parts. Respect safe areas, on-screen
keyboards and touch interactions.

## Boundary and maintenance policy

- One authored source: `src/tokens.css`. All native tokens are generated,
  deterministic and checked by `--check`. No second hand-maintained theme.
- The CSS package's exports and zero-dependency core are **unchanged**.
  Native consumers copy only the files they need; no React, Expo, Flutter,
  Swift or Compose dependencies are added to Syntyr.
- Runtime controls remain genuinely native. Native keyboard navigation,
  gesture handling, accessibility and OS adaptations are not made equivalent
  by colors or spacing alone.
- Native builds have **not** been run by the Syntyr test suite; token/adapter
  contract tests are run in CI or locally. Validate a real iOS/Android app
  before claiming full platform certification.

References: [React Native styles](https://reactnative.dev/docs/style.html),
[Expo Web](https://docs.expo.dev/workflow/web/),
[Expo CSS limitations](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v55.0.0/config/metro/).

---

## Source: docs/native-browser-apis.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/native-browser-apis.md

# Native browser APIs in Syntyr

Syntyr is a styling system, **not** a browser API abstraction layer. It ships no runtime JavaScript or polyfill. Use the browser's built-in semantics and state before adding host-owned JavaScript. See the [scriptless integration demo](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/native-apis.html) (source: `examples/native-apis.html`).

For framework-free custom elements and server-rendered Shadow DOM, see the
[native Web Components fixture](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/tree/main/examples/web-components) and
[component-authoring contract](component-authoring.md). Syntyr still requires
no Custom Elements runtime for ordinary HTML components.

## Supported integrations

| Primitive | Syntyr integration | Fallback / requirement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML Popover API | `.syn-popover` on `[popover]` with `popovertarget`/`popovertargetaction` controls | Native API requires modern browser; critical content should remain reachable another way for older browsers |
| Invoker Commands | `commandfor` and `command="show-modal"` on buttons targeting `.syn-dialog` | Older browsers may not support commands; give an ordinary link or `<details>` alternative |
| Native `<dialog>` | `.syn-dialog`, `form method="dialog"`, `closedby` or app-owned `requestClose()` | Never replace modal semantics with a popover; handle focus on open/close in real-app tests |
| CSS anchor positioning | `.syn-popover--anchored` alongside `.syn-popover` | With `position-area: bottom`, place near its invoking button; otherwise default to visible corner popover |
| Content-sized fields | `.syn-textarea--autosize` alongside `.syn-textarea` | `field-sizing: content` grows to a maximum height; normal resizable textarea remains functional without support |
| CSS scroll-driven animation | `.syn-reading-progress` in optional motion stylesheet | Decorative, hidden without support or with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` |
| Discrete overlay transitions | `.syn-popover--transition` in optional motion stylesheet | Uses `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`; no animation without support or when reduced motion is requested |
| Container queries | `.syn-region` with scoped layout patterns | Native responsive CSS replaces ResizeObserver for layout |
| Form constraint validation | `required`, native types, `:user-invalid` and optional `aria-invalid` | Application must provide meaningful feedback and accessible error text |

All new classes are **opt-in**. Core styles only add the anchor and textarea declarations; optional motion requires `syntyr.motion.css` (included in `syntyr.all.css`). Do not load `syntyr.all.css` alongside component files.

For practical scriptless action panels and an optional enhanced menu adapter, see [dropdown patterns](dropdowns.md).

## Example: popover near its invoker

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="syntyr.motion.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="account-menu">Account</button>
  <div id="account-menu" popover class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored syn-popover--transition">
    <a href="/profile">Profile</a>
    <button type="button" popovertarget="account-menu" popovertargetaction="hide">Close</button>
  </div>
</section>
```

The invoker creates an implicit CSS anchor. Do not apply `position-anchor: auto` to unrelated floating elements; supply an explicit anchor relationship or use normal document positioning. The default `.syn-popover` remains visible in browsers without anchor positioning. Make sure production menus have sensible keyboard navigation and screen-reader labeling.

## Example: a dialog without an event handler

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <button type="button" commandfor="confirm-dialog" command="show-modal">Review</button>
  <dialog id="confirm-dialog" class="syn-dialog" aria-labelledby="confirm-title">
    <h2 id="confirm-title">Review changes</h2>
    <form method="dialog"><button type="submit">Close</button></form>
  </dialog>
</section>
```

The HTML Invoker Commands API is progressively available; don't assume the opener works in legacy browsers. A normal link to a review page or a `<details>` fallback gives users an accessible path even without it. Use `dialog.requestClose()` from host JavaScript when a cancelable close request is needed; unlike `dialog.close()`, `requestClose()` fires `cancel` first.

## Application-owned JavaScript (optional)

The following browser APIs are **not** included as Syntyr runtime dependencies. Use them only for capabilities CSS and HTML cannot provide:

- **View Transition API**: for same-document updates, use `document.startViewTransition(updateDOM)` only if present and if reduced-motion is not preferred; otherwise run `updateDOM()` directly. Cross-document navigation requires explicit `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in *both* same-origin documents, not in a global Syntyr bundle. Preserve focus, history, and scrolling semantics during navigation.
- **Clipboard API**: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)` requires a secure context and permissions/user activation; catch rejections and provide a selectable text/link fallback.
- **Web Share API**: check `navigator.share`, invoke it from a click handler, catch cancellation or errors, and retain an ordinary shareable URL when unavailable. Do not assume mobile-only availability or guaranteed success.
- **ResizeObserver**: reserve for application logic that must know measured dimensions; use CSS container queries for styling. Avoid synchronous DOM changes from observers that trigger resize loops.
- **IntersectionObserver**: use to defer expensive application work, not for effects already supported by `animation-timeline: scroll(root block)`. Prefer native `loading="lazy"` for offscreen images and iframes.
- **Web Animations API**: suitable for interruptible, imperative application animations; use CSS transitions and scroll-driven animations for presentation-only changes and honor reduced motion.
- **Navigation API**: potentially helpful to app routers, but it changes navigation ownership. Do not add it to Syntyr just to style links; ordinary links work without it.

A safe view transition wrapper in application code, not the Syntyr library:

```js
function updateWithViewTransition(updateDOM) {
  if (!document.startViewTransition ||
      matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
    updateDOM();
    return;
  }
  document.startViewTransition(updateDOM);
}
```


## Static semantic validation for native controls

The opt-in Syntyr checker can catch broken HTML relationships before browser testing:

```sh
python3 scripts/syntyr_check.py --semantic examples/native-apis.html
```

In complete, literal HTML documents it verifies explicit `<label for>` targets
are labelable, native `popovertarget`/`commandfor` targets exist, and
`input[list]` points to `<datalist>`. Built-in dialog commands must target
`<dialog>`. Popover command events may dispatch on HTML targets without a
`popover` attribute; unlike `popovertarget`, this is not an error. It also catches
`<summary>` outside a direct `<details>` parent and image submit controls
without an accessible name. These are **HTML correctness** checks; no Syntyr
class is necessary. The checker deliberately leaves references in fragments
and dynamic templates to the consuming application, and allows custom-element
commands without guessing their behavior.

This is not a full HTML, ARIA, accessibility, or browser-conformance validator.
Use the [WHATWG HTML Standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/), an HTML validator,
real browser keyboard and assistive-technology tests, and application-level
validation for server-rendered templates. For a popover, use the declarative
invoker rather than manually adding ARIA expansion state that the browser
already manages; for modal content, use `<dialog>` and a real accessible name.


## Browser-compatibility policy

Test Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit at narrow widths and 200%/400% zoom. CSS feature queries guard anchor placement and scroll-driven timelines. Without the advanced feature, the controls remain styled, dismissible, and operable **where the underlying HTML primitive is supported**. For genuinely older browsers that lack the HTML primitive entirely, provide an alternative interaction or a conditionally loaded host-app polyfill; Syntyr never silently installs one.

Always verify keyboard focus, Escape dismissal, forced-colors mode, native validation, and `prefers-reduced-motion`. Avoid animated content that conveys information unavailable as text. The scroll indicator uses `aria-hidden="true"` and must not replace a semantic progress bar for tasks.

Compatibility references: [Popover API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API), [Invoker Commands](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Invoker_Commands_API), [CSS anchor positioning](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_anchor_positioning), [field-sizing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/field-sizing), [scroll-driven animations](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_scroll-driven_animations), [View Transition API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API).

## Source: docs/dropdowns.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/dropdowns.md

# Dropdowns and selects

Syntyr supplies styling; native HTML owns ordinary behavior. Use the **native** primitive that matches the task rather than treating every popup as a menu.

## Choose the right primitive

| Need | Use | Keyboard | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Select one value in a form | `<select class="syn-select">` | Native select keys | None |
| Open a set of ordinary links/buttons | `[popover].syn-popover.syn-dropdown` | Tab and Escape | None |
| Show expandable information | `<details class="syn-details">` | Native disclosure keys | None |
| Desktop-style application menu | Optional `enhanceMenu()` adapter | ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home, End, typeahead | Explicit opt-in module |
| Select several values in a form | `<select class="syn-select" multiple name="regions">` | Native multi-select keys | None |
| Autocomplete or hierarchical menu | Use an accessible, tested application widget | Full ARIA pattern | App-owned |

The no-JS example is [examples/dropdowns.html](https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/examples/dropdowns.html). The native Popover API provides light dismissal and Escape behavior in supporting browsers. Older browsers need an alternative if the actions are essential.

## Scriptless action panel

```html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="record-actions">Actions</button>
<div id="record-actions" popover class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored syn-dropdown">
  <p class="syn-dropdown__group-label">Record</p>
  <a class="syn-dropdown__item" href="/records/123">View record</a>
  <button type="button" class="syn-dropdown__item" popovertarget="record-actions"
          popovertargetaction="hide">Close</button>
</div>
```

**Do not add `role="menu"` to this pattern.** The browser's normal Tab navigation is intentional. Use buttons for actions and links for navigation. `aria-disabled="true"` alone does not suppress navigation or handlers; use real `disabled` buttons or enforce the disabled condition in the application.

The dropdown CSS supplies compact rows, dividers, group headings, optional keyboard shortcut labels, selected and danger visual treatments, max-block-size scrolling, and a viewport-positioned fallback when anchor positioning is unsupported. Show shortcut hints only for real, implemented keybindings; use `aria-hidden="true"` for redundant decorative key glyphs.

## Customizable native select (experimental)

```html
<label class="syn-label" for="region">Region
  <select id="region" name="region" class="syn-select syn-select--enhanced">
    <option value="north">North</option><option value="south">South</option>
  </select>
</label>
```

The opt-in `base-select` appearance and `::picker(select)` styles are wrapped in `@supports (appearance: base-select)`. They do not replace the element or its value/submission semantics. Test the actual browser/OS/version you support; custom picker rendering is not uniform across engines. Do not expect arbitrary option markup to work everywhere.

## Optional application menu adapter

Only enable this if an application needs WAI-ARIA menu keyboard interactions. This module is **not loaded by the CSS**, and importing it does not auto-initialize menus.

```html
<button type="button" class="syn-button" popovertarget="editor-menu">Editor actions</button>
<div id="editor-menu" popover data-syn-menu aria-label="Editor actions"
     class="syn-popover syn-popover--anchored syn-dropdown">
  <button type="button" class="syn-dropdown__item" data-syn-menu-item>Rename</button>
  <button type="button" class="syn-dropdown__item" data-syn-menu-item>Duplicate</button>
  <button type="button" class="syn-dropdown__item" data-syn-menu-item disabled>Archive</button>
</div>
<script type="module">
  // Copy the exported menu.mjs to your public/assets directory.
  import { enhanceMenu } from '/assets/syntyr-menu.mjs';
  const dispose = enhanceMenu(document.getElementById('editor-menu'));
  // Call dispose() if the host framework unmounts this menu.
</script>
```

The browser-resolvable URL above assumes you have copied the exported
integrations/dropdown/menu.mjs to /assets/syntyr-menu.mjs in your application.
When using a bundler instead, import from the package subpath
@syntyr/css/menu.mjs. Neither path is automatically installed as a public
URL by the CSS framework. The adapter rejects popover="manual" because
manual popovers do not natively dismiss on Escape.

The adapter sets and restores the trigger's `aria-haspopup`, `aria-controls`, and `aria-expanded` attributes. It enables `role="menu"`, menuitem semantics, ArrowDown/ArrowUp navigation, Home/End, typeahead, and initial focus only after it starts. Without JavaScript, the same markup remains a normal set of tabbable controls. Escape uses native popover dismissal. Checkboxes, radio groups, nested submenus and searchable comboboxes are **not** provided; don't use their ARIA roles without implementing and testing their full behavior.

## QA checklist

Test at 320px and 400% zoom, with long translated labels, RTL direction, touch, keyboard-only Tab / Shift+Tab / Escape, and screen reader announcements (NVDA/Firefox, VoiceOver/Safari, or Orca/Firefox). Check selected/disabled items, forced colors, reduced motion, multiple simultaneous menus, and near-viewport-edge anchor placement. Automated assertions are necessary but not a substitute for manual screen reader review.

---

## Source: docs/theme-customization.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/theme-customization.md

# Syntyr theme customization — copy, override, ship

Syntyr themes are **CSS custom properties**, not JavaScript configuration.
The MIT core already includes Grid and Noir palettes, responsive primitives,
accessible focus styling and semantic element options.

## 1. Choose a theme

Without a `data-syn-theme` attribute, `.syn-root` now uses Studio. Select Grid or Noir explicitly for technical/cinematic styles. This change is only in the unreleased alpha.5 candidate; version-pinned alpha.4 assets remain unchanged.

Load the published `syntyr.core.css` in your application and use regular HTML:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut">
    <h2 class="syn-heading">Sector status</h2>
    <button class="syn-button syn-button--primary">Open</button>
  </article>
  <aside data-syn-theme="noir" class="syn-panel">
    Nested Noir preview
  </aside>
</section>
```

Use `data-syn-theme="noir"` for warm amber. Native HTML features
such as `details`, `dialog` and `popover` don't need framework JavaScript.

## Copyable theme presets (alpha.5 documentation tool)

The [theme editor](theme-editor.html) now previews independently selectable
theme, visual intensity, control density, and radius, and generates both CSS
overrides and a portable JSON preset. Copy the JSON into an application-owned
design configuration or use the CSS immediately. The JSON is declarative
metadata, not an executable preset installer, stylesheet, or published API.
For density/intensity, apply the indicated `data-syn-density` and
`data-syn-intensity` attributes on the Syntyr scope. A custom radius uses
`--syn-radius` and `--syn-panel-radius`; the default option preserves each
base theme's geometry. The documentation script and clipboard enhancement are
not included in Syntyr's distributed CSS. Test the resulting palette and
control contrast in the consuming application.

## 2. Override tokens using application CSS

Syntyr declares its defaults in named cascade layers. App CSS without a
layer takes precedence over layered author rules regardless of selector specificity.
Load application overrides **after** the Syntyr stylesheet to reduce surprises:

```css
/* app.css: original tokens, not copied from existing entertainment IP. */
.syn-root[data-syn-theme="grid"] {
  --syn-accent: #80dfef;
  --syn-on-accent: #07121a;
  --syn-accent-soft: rgb(128 223 239 / 10%);
  --syn-frame: #34576c;
}

/* Override one nested region without affecting the rest of the site. */
.my-warning-panel {
  --syn-surface: #1b232d;
  --syn-warning: #ffe2aa;
}
```

Important: `--syn-accent` is the most visible token, but `--syn-on-accent`
is the contrasting **foreground on primary buttons**. Change both when
necessary. Verify 4.5:1 contrast for body text and 3:1 for essential non-text
graphics; don't assume arbitrary overrides remain accessible.

Primary-button hover backgrounds default to the unchanged accent. On hover,
the border switches to the contrasting foreground for a visible affordance.
To customize the hover fill, set `--syn-primary-hover-bg` on the desired
theme/root and test its contrast with `--syn-on-accent` in both rest and hover
states. Syntyr does not automatically invent a contrast-safe hover color.

Use `.syn-panel--raised` for opt-in elevation. The `.syn-title`/`.syn-display`
and `.syn-section-heading` roles use native `text-wrap: balance` when
supported; unsupported browsers fall back to ordinary line wrapping.
Syntyr leaves platform font smoothing untouched.

Useful tokens:

| Token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-bg` | Main background |
| `--syn-surface`, `--syn-surface-hi` | Cards and controls |
| `--syn-text`, `--syn-muted` | Main and secondary text |
| `--syn-accent`, `--syn-on-accent`, `--syn-accent-soft` | Brand accent, its foreground, soft fill |
| `--syn-frame`, `--syn-danger`, `--syn-success`, `--syn-warning` | Borders and status |
| `--syn-font`, `--syn-mono`, `--syn-font-ui`, `--syn-font-display` | Body, technical, control, and display typography |
| `--syn-type-xs`, `--syn-type-sm`, `--syn-type-base` | Typography sizes |
| `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, `--syn-border-subtle` | Derived surfaces and quiet separators |
| `--syn-text-subtle`, `--syn-border-default`, `--syn-border-hover`, `--syn-border-focus`, `--syn-focus-ring` | Semantic text, borders, and focus |
| `--syn-surface-interactive`, `--syn-surface-hover`, `--syn-surface-pressed` | Theme-aware interactive control states |
| `--syn-primary-hover-bg` | Primary-button hover background; defaults to the accent so foreground contrast does not regress |
| `--syn-shadow-sm`, `--syn-shadow-raised`, `--syn-shadow-overlay` | Semantic elevation (small surfaces, raised panels, floating overlays) |
| `--syn-type-display`, `--syn-type-section`, `--syn-type-heading`, `--syn-type-body`, `--syn-leading-body`, `--syn-tracking-display` | Composable typography roles |
| `--syn-row-padding-block`, `--syn-card-padding`, `--syn-control-padding-block` | Density-aware spacing |
| `--syn-space-1` … `--syn-space-5` | Spacing |
| `--syn-cut`, `--syn-radius`, `--syn-control-height` | Geometry |
| `--syn-duration-fast`, `--syn-duration-standard`, `--syn-ease`, `--syn-ease-enter` | Optional transitions |
| `--syn-panel-padding`, `--syn-panel-radius`, `--syn-panel-border-width` | Local panel customization |
| `--syn-button-padding-inline`, `--syn-button-border-width` | Local button customization |

## 3. Independent visual intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity="quiet"` on a dense dashboard, the default `standard` for a balanced presentation, or `cinematic` on a limited hero region. Intensity controls only opt-in decoration in `syntyr.effects.css`; it does not alter palette, density, typography or control contrast. Nested regions can override an inherited value. See the [visual-intensity guide](visual-intensity.md) and [live comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html).

## 4. CSS component mode versus native semantic mode

Scoped component classes: `.syn-panel`, `.syn-button`, `.syn-table`.
They work with only `syntyr.core.css`.

For classless HTML resembling Pico CSS, load **both** files and opt in:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.semantic.css">
<div class="syn-root syn-semantic" data-syn-theme="noir">
  <article>
    <h2>Operator access</h2>
    <label for="operator">Operator ID</label>
    <input id="operator" name="operator" required>
    <button>Continue</button>
  </article>
</div>
```

Unclassed controls outside `.syn-semantic` are not restyled.
If you need glows or static grid effects, add `syntyr.effects.css`
as a third optional file. Don't load `syntyr.all.css` **and** its
individual component files at the same time.

## 5. Responsive applications and accessibility

Use `.syn-region` as the parent for container-responsive patterns such as
`.syn-stats`, `.syn-split`, `.syn-pricing`; width comes from the container,
not the whole viewport. Use `.syn-page` only for a full-page experience.

Syntyr also honors `prefers-contrast: more` by strengthening tokenized borders
and suppressing nonessential decorative effects, including inside nested
themes and explicit cinematic-intensity regions. This is a preference-aware
visual enhancement, not a substitute for actual high-contrast/forced-colors,
zoom, and screen-reader testing.

Syntyr honors `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Theme overrides
must not remove focus outlines, fake disabled states, or communicate state
only through color. Test keyboard navigation, 200%/400% browser zoom,
high-contrast/forced-colors, and relevant screen readers in the target app.

**No runtime JavaScript is required for styling.** Search, authentication,
live data, and server-side form handling are intentionally application
responsibilities; optional advanced widgets are outside the CSS core.

## Seven theme palettes (unreleased alpha.5 candidate)

The published alpha.4 tag offers Grid, Noir and Studio. This candidate adds Industrial, Terminal, Corporate and Minimal. Use the same HTML and change only the theme attribute:

- `data-syn-theme="grid"`
- `data-syn-theme="noir"`
- `data-syn-theme="studio"`
- `data-syn-theme="industrial"`
- `data-syn-theme="terminal"`
- `data-syn-theme="corporate"`
- `data-syn-theme="minimal"`

To use finite opt-in layout utilities, load `syntyr.utilities.css` after `syntyr.core.css` (or use the all bundle). Utilities include `.syn-u-flex`, `.syn-u-grid`, `.syn-u-between`, spacing helpers and a visually hidden helper. No compiler or runtime JavaScript is required.


## System palette, no JavaScript (experimental)

`data-syn-theme="auto"` on `.syn-root` or a nested themed region
uses Studio colors for light system preference and Grid colors for dark
system preference. It relies on native `color-scheme: light dark` and
CSS `light-dark()`, supported by current Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
Older engines that lack `light-dark()` retain the inherited/default
palette. No preference is stored or read by Syntyr.

```html
<body class="syn-root syn-page" data-syn-theme="auto">
  <section data-syn-theme="noir">This remains Noir regardless of OS theme.</section>
</body>
```

Explicit palettes are unchanged. For sensitive applications, test nested
themes, native form controls, and contrast in both OS preference modes.
## Typography, density, and quiet surfaces

Control and navigation text uses `--syn-font-ui`. Display headings use
`--syn-font-display`, while code and CLI regions retain `--syn-mono`.
Grid and Terminal choose monospace UI explicitly; Studio is the implicit default; light themes and Noir use
system sans-serif controls. Replace the font variables if a product has its
own typeface, without introducing required external fonts.

The `--syn-surface-recessed`, `--syn-surface-raised`, and
`--syn-border-subtle` tokens derive from the active theme palette and
recompute in nested themed regions. Strong borders remain available for
focus and essential controls. Avoid treating subtle separators as a substitute
for accessible non-text contrast where boundaries are required.

To opt into compact operational layouts:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="minimal" data-syn-density="compact">
  <table class="syn-table"><!-- ... semantic rows ... --></table>
</section>
```

Compact density reduces padding and control heights, **not font sizes**.
Use the default density for content-heavy business pages or touch-first forms.
For an optional editorial hero, combine `syn-site-heading--editorial` from
`syntyr.recipes.css` with `syn-gradient-wash` from `syntyr.effects.css`.
Both use local fonts and static CSS without runtime dependencies.


## Semantic roles, states, and content rhythm

Use `.syn-display` (also available as `.syn-title`), `.syn-section-heading` for section titles, `.syn-heading` for card headings,
`.syn-body`, `.syn-text-support`, and the opt-in `.syn-prose` content
container. Typography roles inherit theme fonts and allow applications to
override type scale without rewriting individual component selectors.

Semantic aliases are derived separately in each nested `data-syn-theme`
scope, so a Grid panel inside a Studio page retains Grid's own contrast and
control appearance. To override theme colors, prefer changing the primitive
palette (`--syn-accent`, `--syn-frame`, `--syn-surface`, etc.). Override a
semantic role only when the change is intentional and contrast has been checked.

Native `disabled`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-busy`,
`:focus-visible`, and `:active` styles are presentation only. `aria-busy`
does not stop clicks or run a task. Use actual `disabled` for disabled form
controls; `aria-disabled` requires the application to suppress activation.
For errors, pair `aria-invalid="true"` with an associated error message
(`aria-describedby`); never rely on border color alone.

See [the live design-state example](../examples/design-states.html) for
semantic typography, nested themes, compact layout and form states.

## Component-local layouts without compilation (experimental alpha.5)

Modern CSS custom properties allow Syntyr to expose a small set of layout
adjustments without inventing more utility classes. The default styles remain
unchanged when you do not provide an override. Consumers need **no build step**,
Tailwind compiler or JavaScript: use a normal stylesheet and optional application
CSS, or put a local variable on a single component.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-grid" style="--syn-grid-min: 14rem; --syn-grid-gap: 1.25rem">
    <article class="syn-panel">Summary</article>
    <article class="syn-panel">Campaigns</article>
    <article class="syn-panel">Revenue</article>
  </div>
</section>
```

Core layout hooks (each can also be set in application CSS):

| Component | Local token | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.syn-grid` | `--syn-grid-min` / `--syn-grid-gap` | `17rem` / `1rem` |
| `.syn-layout` | `--syn-layout-min` / `--syn-layout-gap` | `21rem` / `1.25rem` |
| `.syn-stack` | `--syn-stack-gap` | `--syn-space-3` |
| `.syn-inline` | `--syn-inline-gap` | `--syn-space-2` |

Optional `syntyr.recipes.css` adds `.syn-kpi-grid`
(`--syn-kpi-min`, `--syn-kpi-gap`), `.syn-filter-bar`
(`--syn-filter-gap`), `.syn-filter-field`
(`--syn-filter-field-min`, `--syn-filter-query-min` on query variants),
and the `.syn-detail-layout` shell (`--syn-detail-gap`,
`--syn-detail-main-basis`, `--syn-detail-main-min`,
`--syn-detail-aside-basis`, `--syn-detail-aside-min`).

```html
<form class="syn-filter-bar" action="/campaigns" method="get"
      style="--syn-filter-gap: 1rem; --syn-filter-field-min: 9rem">
  <label class="syn-filter-field">
    Status
    <select class="syn-select" name="status">
      <option value="">All statuses</option>
      <option>Active</option>
    </select>
  </label>
  <button class="syn-button" type="submit">Filter</button>
</form>
```

Intrinsic grids and wrapping filter/detail layouts respond to their available
width, including inside narrow application panels. An explicit named
`.syn-region` container remains the contract for components using
`@container syn-region`. Do not set implausible minimum widths or nonlength
values: a CSS variable with an invalid value can invalidate its entire
declaration despite the `var()` fallback.

## Native state styling and accessibility

The classed `.syn-field` adds a focus-within label cue. Its label switches to
the danger color when it contains an `aria-invalid="true"` control or a
user-invalid native control. `.syn-input-group` highlights its addon border
when a child receives focus. Core `.syn-panel[inert]` uses a dashed border and
recessed surface to indicate unavailability, while the browser supplies inert
interaction semantics. Use `inert` on the actual unavailable subtree, not as
a substitute for server authorization; when not native or when unsupported,
styling alone cannot disable behavior.

Always preserve real labels, associated error text and focus outlines. For
invalid fields, provide an error message and connect it with
`aria-describedby`. The styling does not perform validation, keyboard
management, popover activation or announcements, and accessibility requires
manual keyboard, zoom, forced-colors and assistive-technology testing.

## Experimental opt-in OKLCH mixing

Syntyr's seven palette primitives and text/foreground contrast pairs remain
unchanged. To compare perceptual color mixing on an individual theme region,
opt in to `data-syn-color-space="oklch"`:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio"
         data-syn-color-space="oklch">
  <button class="syn-button">Perceptual surface hover</button>
  <aside data-syn-theme="grid" data-syn-color-space="oklch">
    Nested themes must opt in independently.
  </aside>
</section>
```

Only the **`--syn-surface-hover`** role uses OKLCH mixing in this experiment.
The default stays in sRGB. Browser engines lacking the required
`color-mix(in oklch, ...)` support retain the existing sRGB role. **Nested themes**
recompute their own tokens; add the opt-in attribute to each theme scope
you intentionally want to compare. Do not generalize this experiment to text
colors or primary buttons without a contrast audit, and check the resulting
hover backgrounds against text across all palettes and browser engines.

---

## Source: docs/visual-intensity.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/visual-intensity.md

# Visual intensity and composable cyberpunk frames

SYNTYR separates **palette** (`data-syn-theme`), **decorative intensity**
(`data-syn-intensity`), **density** (`data-syn-density`) and optional geometry
(`.syn-frame` plus one shape). These are independent controls and do not load
JavaScript, fonts, sprites or third-party assets.

## Choose the right intensity

Use `data-syn-intensity` on `.syn-root` or any descendant element. It is
inherited, so a child can opt into a different intensity without switching
palette. Omitting the attribute is equivalent to `standard`.

| Value | Effects | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quiet` | Nearly invisible grids/washes; no visible glow/scanline overlay | Data-heavy SaaS, forms, accessibility-sensitive dashboards |
| `standard` | Existing effect strengths and opt-in behavior (default) | Marketing sites, documentation |
| `cinematic` | Stronger washes, luminous shadows and optional scanlines | Demos, editorial hero sections, limited promotional panels |

Intensity changes **only opt-in decorative effects** from
`syntyr.effects.css`. It does not change status colors, border contrast,
focus rings, typography, form affordances or any theme's underlying palette.
For zero decoration, simply do not load effects.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.effects.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">

<main class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid" data-syn-intensity="quiet">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-glow">
    <h2>Operational view</h2>
    <p>Quiet default for dense data.</p>
  </article>
  <section data-syn-intensity="cinematic">
    <article class="syn-panel syn-glow syn-frame syn-frame--bevel syn-frame--accent">
      <h2>Featured transmission</h2>
      <p>A localized visual accent without changing colors or density.</p>
    </article>
  </section>
</main>
```

For custom presets, override `--syn-grid-alpha`, `--syn-glow-alpha`,
`--syn-wash-alpha`, `--syn-wash-secondary-alpha`,
`--syn-horizon-alpha`, and `--syn-scanline-alpha` on a region.
Values are percentages used in color interpolation, not animation speed.
Cinematic does **not** animate automatically; use optional motion modules
separately and respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## Geometry that composes

The optional `syntyr.geometry.css` stylesheet supports five shapes:
`bevel`, `notch`, `bracket`, `inset` and `circuit`.
Use exactly one shape on `.syn-frame`, optionally adding
`.syn-frame--accent` for a stronger outline (2px accent-colored border).
The geometry layer explicitly resets pseudo-element dimensions and clipping
from earlier CSS layers, so `.syn-panel--cut` on the **same host** is safely
superseded by the selected frame geometry rather than corrupting it.

```html
<article class="syn-panel syn-panel--cut syn-frame syn-frame--notch syn-frame--accent">
  <h2>System status</h2>
  <p>The notch frame takes precedence over the simpler panel cut.</p>
</article>
```

`syn-frame--accent` is an *optional* style modifier, not an additional
shape. Set `--syn-frame-cut`, `--syn-frame-stroke`,
`--syn-frame-fill` or `--syn-frame-outline` on the host to customize
one frame. Avoid combining two shape modifiers.

**Remaining composability boundary:** both `syn-frame` geometry and the
older `syn-frame--precision` recipe own `::before`. Applying both
to the same host still supersedes the precision accent; nest separate
elements when both treatments are needed. Likewise, geometry intentionally
uses a transparent host background so gradients painted on the **host**
may spill into its cut corners. Apply complex host backgrounds on an inner
element, or set `--syn-frame-fill` to a solid value.

## Accessibility and performance

- Always keep readable status text; never communicate errors only by glow or color.
- In forced-colors mode, frames fall back to solid system borders and effects
  suppress nonessential backgrounds.
- Prefer `quiet` for long operational pages; reserve `cinematic` for a few
  deliberate accents. Measure paint and scrolling on actual devices.
- The library core does not require any script. The optional docs theme editor
  can preview intensity but is not shipped as an application dependency.
- Test with 200% and 400% zoom, keyboard input, forced colors and all three
  browser engines before relying on a theme in production.

See [live intensity comparison](../examples/intensity-geometry.html),
[advanced geometry](geometry-terminal.md) and
[theme customization](theme-customization.md).

---

## Source: docs/visual-composition.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/visual-composition.md

# Syntyr visual composition — premium restraint, distinct character

This guide applies original layout decisions informed by the **principles**
publicly described by Resend, Vercel, Linear, Raycast and PostHog. Do not copy
their proprietary brand marks, code, fonts, illustrations, components or layouts.
The Syntyr CSS public contract stays independent and MIT licensed.

## Product-led presentation

- Show a real HTML/CSS component next to the markup used to construct it.
  Annotate fictional data honestly; never imply a static mockup is a live app.
- Use one dominant action and one secondary action in the first viewport.
  Move tertiary exploration paths to the next relevant section.
- Give each page one descriptive `h1`, readable section headings, and a clear
  keyboard-first navigation path. Do not rely on visual headings alone.

## Surface and typography rules

1. Prefer **one visible boundary per edge**. When nested surfaces both have
   borders, use `--syn-border-subtle` for internal dividers and reserve
   `--syn-frame` / `--syn-frame-strong` for controls and meaningful edges.
2. Apply depth sparingly. A raised overlay may use `--syn-shadow-overlay`;
   routine dashboard cards should rely on spacing and role separation first.
3. Use `--syn-font-ui` for ordinary controls, `--syn-font-display` for
   headings and `--syn-mono` for technical data. The optional system-serif
   editorial recipe should not bleed into operational controls.
4. Prefer sentence case for Studio, Minimal and Corporate UI. Technical
   uppercase labels are intentional in Grid and Terminal, not the default.
5. Use `--syn-accent` for real actions, selection, and a few signature
   details. Do not color every title, border, metric and icon at once.

## Same components, three visual directions

- [Studio operations](../examples/flagship-studio.html): compact density,
  unambiguous tables, quiet cards and a clear action order.
- [Noir editorial](../examples/flagship-noir.html): system serif, atmospheric
  background on one section, generous white space, restrained warm accents.
- [Grid control](../examples/flagship-grid.html): precise geometric framing,
  sparse cyan highlights, legible operational records and explicitly simulated
  output. Opt into cinematic effects only on a contained hero.

These are **documentation-only compositions**. Their `flagship.css` file is
application-owned showcase styling, not an additional required Syntyr module.

## Accessibility, motion and maintenance

- Maintain visible focus indicators and appropriate contrast for meaningful
  text and control boundaries; never depend on color, glow, or tiny labels alone.
- The data or state must still make sense at 320px and 400% zoom. Wide tables
  may scroll in a labeled, keyboard-focusable region.
- Suppress nonessential effects under forced-colors; respect reduced motion.
  Avoid perpetual `will-change`, large blur layers and decorative timers.
- Favor CSS custom properties and existing `syn-*` classes over bespoke
  component forks. Keep theme, density, intensity, and geometry independent.
- Measure real browser rendering and review screenshots before making
  visual regressions a release gate.

## References

Public design reading:
- [Resend brand guidelines](https://resend.com/handbook/design/what-are-our-brand-guidelines)
- [Linear design refresh](https://linear.app/now/behind-the-latest-design-refresh)
- [Vercel Geist design system](https://vercel.com/geist/introduction)

See also [theme customization](theme-customization.md),
[visual intensity](visual-intensity.md), and
[design research](design-research-linear-resend.md).

## Source: docs/geometry-terminal.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/geometry-terminal.md

# Advanced frames and terminal presentation

These are original, MIT-licensed SYNTYR CSS components. They do not replicate entertainment franchise assets or require JavaScript.

## Installation

Load only the modules you need. Advanced geometry is separate so ordinary pages do not load its CSS:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">
<!-- Only for the optional application/terminal layouts: -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.recipes.css">
```

The all-in-one stylesheet includes geometry and recipes already. Do not load it alongside the individual modules.

## Seven independent frame profiles

Use `.syn-frame` with exactly **one** shape modifier. These can decorate an article, section, or any normal element. The surrounding content stays semantic:

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-frame syn-frame--bevel" style="--syn-frame-cut: 1.5rem">
    <h2>Monitoring</h2>
    <p>All systems operational.</p>
    <a href="/status">See status</a>
  </article>
</section>
```

| Class | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-frame--bevel` | Diagonal cut on all four corners |
| `.syn-frame--notch` | Asymmetric top-right and bottom-left cuts |
| `.syn-frame--step` | Square stepped cuts on top-right and bottom-left |
| `.syn-frame--facet` | Diagonal cuts on top-left and bottom-right |
| `.syn-frame--bracket` | Four HUD-style L-shaped corner markers |
| `.syn-frame--inset` | Nested technical border |
| `.syn-frame--circuit` | Subtle corner trace bars |

These style variables are inherited and can be overridden on a specific panel:

- `--syn-frame-cut`: default `1rem`; fallback size for all cuts (backwards-compatible)
- `--syn-frame-cut-tl`, `--syn-frame-cut-tr`, `--syn-frame-cut-br`, `--syn-frame-cut-bl`: optional **Per-corner** overrides; use explicit CSS lengths
- `--syn-frame-stroke`: default `1px`; border thickness for clipped shapes
- `--syn-frame-fill`: default `var(--syn-surface)`; interior background
- `--syn-frame-outline`: default `var(--syn-frame-strong)`; solid border fallback
- `--syn-frame-border-paint`: optional color or CSS gradient for the complete border
- `--syn-frame-inlay-paint`: optional CSS gradient layered over the inner fill; use a translucent wash

The clipped shapes use individually corrected inner polygons to keep diagonal borders closer to their specified perpendicular stroke width. Square steps use the same step size for both polygons. These are **painted frames**, not clipped interactive hit regions; the native element remains a rectangle for layout and focus. Avoid cut sizes larger than the element can accommodate, or strokes as large as the cuts.

### Asymmetric geometry and gradient border example

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geometry.css">
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="grid">
  <article class="syn-panel syn-frame syn-frame--facet" style="
    --syn-frame-cut-tl: 1.5rem; --syn-frame-cut-br: .75rem;
    --syn-frame-stroke: 2px;
    --syn-frame-border-paint: linear-gradient(120deg, var(--syn-accent), var(--syn-frame-strong));
    --syn-frame-inlay-paint: linear-gradient(145deg, rgb(118 231 247 / 7%), transparent 65%);
  ">
    <h2>Signal analysis</h2>
    <p>Decorative geometry never replaces semantic content.</p>
  </article>
</section>
```

For the interactive **geometry editor**, open [Syntyr's component playground](playground.html#geometry-title). The playground JavaScript is documentation-only; consumers load only CSS. Existing bevel/notch markup retains its original appearance unless new controls are set, apart from the improved diagonal stroke geometry.

**Composition:** Advanced frame profiles own both pseudo-elements of the host node. They now reset the prior layer's corner dimensions and clip-path, so `.syn-panel--cut` can be used on the same element: the selected frame shape **supersedes** its simpler corner decoration. Add `.syn-frame--accent` for a stronger outline without adding any pseudo-elements. Do not combine multiple shape variants. The older `.syn-frame--precision` also owns `::before`; nest those two treatments if both accents must remain visible. The clipped border geometry does not depend on matching the parent background, but background gradients on the host can bleed into cut corners; prefer solid `--syn-frame-fill` or an inner element.

In forced-colors mode, decorative pseudo-elements disappear and a visible native border and Canvas background take over. Frames should not be the only way you communicate operational state.

## Browser terminal

Load `syntyr.recipes.css` for the existing `.syn-terminal` base and the additional presentation classes:

| Class | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `.syn-terminal-bar`, `.syn-terminal-title`, `.syn-terminal-dots` | Window chrome; mark visual-only dots `aria-hidden="true"` |
| `.syn-terminal-body`, `.syn-terminal-line`, `.syn-terminal-output` | Readable lines, wrapped output |
| `.syn-terminal-command`, `.syn-terminal-path`, `.syn-terminal-prompt` | CLI command anatomy |
| `.syn-terminal-success`, `.syn-terminal-warning`, `.syn-terminal-error` | Colored output (with textual status) |
| `.syn-terminal-meta`, `.syn-terminal-muted` | Secondary readouts |
| `.syn-terminal-cursor` | Static decorative caret; hide from accessibility APIs |

The terminal is **not** a shell emulator. It performs no input capture or commands. Applications implement real interaction separately; native CLI applications use `terminal/palettes.json` rather than browser CSS.

## Table and button behavior

The existing `.syn-table-emphasis` class highlights whichever cell you choose: there is no implicit highlight on the last column. Use `.syn-cell--numeric` on monetary or numeric cells for right-aligned tabular numbers.

The native HTML `disabled` attribute blocks button activation. The ARIA `aria-disabled="true"` attribute only communicates a disabled state; it **does not block activation**. Application/server code must enforce disabled behavior. CSS alone cannot guarantee it. For a disabled action that must remain discoverable to keyboard users, preserve focus and handle input appropriately.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py
python3 scripts/build.py --check
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 tests/browser_matrix.py --browsers chromium firefox webkit
```

See [the frame + terminal example](../examples/geometry-terminal.html). Browser checks are developer-only; the distributed CSS still has zero runtime JS or dependencies.

## Source: docs/viz.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/viz.md

# Syntyr Viz: optional, renderer-neutral charts

`syntyr.viz.css` is an **optional CSS-only presentation module**. It styles
charts and small, server-renderable data visualizations in all seven Syntyr
themes. It does not compute chart geometry, ingest data, perform interactions,
supply a JavaScript runtime, or require a frontend framework.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.viz.css">
```

Alternatively load `syntyr.all.css` by itself. Do **not** load the all-in-one
bundle together with component modules: it already includes Viz. Core, the
convenience `syntyr.css` bundle, and the optional recipes stylesheet do not
contain Viz.

## Chart token API

All visualization colors are CSS variables. Their defaults recompute on
`.syn-root` and nested `[data-syn-theme]` containers.

| Token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `--syn-chart-1` through `--syn-chart-4` | Data series colors, derived from theme accent, secondary accent, success, warning |
| `--syn-chart-grid` | Grid and chart cell border color |
| `--syn-chart-axis` | Axis labels and marks |
| `--syn-chart-tooltip-bg` | Noninteractive tooltip/popup surface |

Override the tokens on a specific themed chart or a nested dashboard area.
Always check contrast and series distinguishability after palette changes.
Color is not an adequate standalone representation of categories or status.
Use text, patterns, line types, legends and accessible values.

```html
<section class="syn-root" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <figure class="syn-chart" style="--syn-chart-1: #2458c6;">
    <figcaption class="syn-chart-title">Weekly signups</figcaption>
    <!-- Supply SVG, a server-side renderer, or a client chart here. -->
  </figure>
</section>
```

## Four microvisualizations

### 1. SVG sparkline

`syn-viz-sparkline` styles a precomputed inline SVG. Syntyr does not calculate
points. For a time series, the HTML generator computes the polyline/area and
includes an accessible name. Use SVG `<title>` or `aria-label` and make the
numerical values inspectable in a nearby table or list.

```html
<figure class="syn-chart">
  <figcaption class="syn-chart-title">Revenue, Jan–Jun</figcaption>
  <svg class="syn-viz-sparkline" viewBox="0 0 240 60" role="img"
       aria-label="Revenue increased from 20 to 54 thousand dollars">
    <polyline class="syn-viz-sparkline-path"
              points="2,54 49,44 96,46 143,24 190,20 238,5"/>
  </svg>
  <table class="syn-table">
    <caption>Revenue by month, thousands of dollars</caption>
    <thead><tr><th scope="col">Month</th><th scope="col">Revenue</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody><tr><th scope="row">Jan</th><td>20</td></tr>
           <tr><th scope="row">Jun</th><td>54</td></tr></tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

### 2. Ranked bar list

Use real text for values; the bar widths are visual duplicates of the
values. `--syn-viz-value` is a number on a 0–100 scale, not a percentage
string. The CSS clamps it into that interval. **Validate and escape values
at the rendering boundary.** This is presentation only, not a semantic
`progress` or `meter` control.

```html
<ol class="syn-viz-bars" aria-label="Revenue mix">
  <li class="syn-viz-bar">
    <div class="syn-viz-bar-label">
      <span>Direct</span><data value="72">72%</data>
    </div>
    <div class="syn-viz-bar-track" aria-hidden="true">
      <span class="syn-viz-bar-fill" style="--syn-viz-value: 72"></span>
    </div>
  </li>
</ol>
```

### 3. Status tracker

This represents a series of discrete periods, not a live network monitor.
Each segment needs **real semantic text** even when a screen reader reads
its visual color differently.

```html
<ol class="syn-viz-tracker" aria-label="Past three days">
  <li data-syn-state="healthy"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Mon: Healthy</span></li>
  <li data-syn-state="degraded"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Tue: Degraded</span></li>
  <li data-syn-state="down"><span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Wed: Down</span></li>
</ol>
<p>Healthy, degraded and down states appear in chronological order.</p>
```

Supported state values are `healthy`, `degraded`, `down`, and `unknown`.
Do not depend on color alone to convey a critical state.

### 4. Activity heatmap

The heatmap is a compact grid. Set `--syn-viz-columns` to the number of
columns; each cell uses one of five levels, `0` through `4`.
The default is twelve columns. For small screens, the grid scrolls rather
than reducing each cell below its minimum width.

```html
<div class="syn-viz-heatmap" style="--syn-viz-columns: 3;"
     role="group" aria-label="Three days of activity">
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="0">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Mon: no activity</span>
  </span>
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="2">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Tue: medium activity</span>
  </span>
  <span class="syn-viz-cell" data-syn-level="4">
    <span class="syn-viz-sr-only">Wed: very high activity</span>
  </span>
</div>
```

## Generic chart styling and integrations

`syn-chart`, `syn-chart-title`, `syn-chart-grid`, `syn-chart-axis`,
`syn-chart-legend`, `syn-chart-legend-item`, `syn-chart-key` and
`syn-chart-tooltip` are **styling hooks only**. They never calculate axes,
create a legend, open a tooltip, or attach event handlers.

- **SVG/server-side:** generate SVG paths and visible, textual value tables
  with Go, Rust, HTMX, Python or any HTML renderer. All functionality remains
  available with no JavaScript.
- **Recharts:** set `className="syn-chart"` on your container and pass
  `var(--syn-chart-1)` etc. into the renderer's stroke/fill props. Use
  native Recharts tooltips/accessibility rather than expecting CSS to
  provide interactions.
- **ECharts:** ECharts needs resolved color strings in its JavaScript
  options, not literal CSS `var()` strings (Canvas cannot interpret them).
  Resolve scoped computed custom properties **inside an optional application
  adapter** and update them if the theme changes. Syntyr does not ship that
  adapter or make it a dependency.

## Accessibility and performance

Keep a visible title, visible value labels where possible, and a navigable
HTML table, list, or accessible summary for the underlying values. Verify
screen reader announcements, high-contrast/forced-colors mode, keyboard
navigation, and 200–400% zoom. Decorative SVG should be `aria-hidden` only
when equivalent numerical information exists elsewhere; meaningful SVG must
have a readable accessible name. Labels and patterns must distinguish status
independently of hue. The CSS includes forced-colors distinctions; test them
on the target browser rather than assuming automatic compliance.

All CSS is scoped under `.syn-root` and deliberately has no network assets,
fonts, animations, script tags or client-side data transforms. Syntyr Viz does
not impose arbitrary CSS size budgets. Use the library's existing deterministic
build and performance tests and measure real browser behavior.

Try the [seven-theme static Viz gallery](../examples/viz.html).

## Source: docs/geo.md

Original: https://syntyr-css.pages.dev/docs/geo.md

# Syntyr Geo — renderer-neutral geospatial interface styles

**Status:** experimental and unreleased. The MIT-licensed `syntyr.geo.css` module styles geospatial application **chrome**: map workspaces, filters, layers, marker hit targets, selected states, clusters, legends, callouts, scale bars and attribution. No JavaScript, tiles, mapping SDK, fonts, or network assets are included in Syntyr Geo. Load `syntyr.core.css` first.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.core.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/css/syntyr.geo.css">
```

Or, in a package-manager application consuming the **unpublished** alpha.5 candidate, import `@syntyr/css/geo.css`. The `syntyr.all.css` bundle already contains Geo; **do not load both**. Neither `syntyr.core.css` nor `syntyr.viz.css` includes it.

**[Open the synthetic, offline Geo demo](../examples/geo.html)**. It is a Schematic illustration, **Not to scale**, with fictional records, no tile provider or API keys, and disabled zoom controls. It is not a map renderer.

### Optional Python standard-library operations demo (repository source)

The [runnable Geo operations server](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/examples/geo_operations_server.py) illustrates **actual server-owned GET filtering and selection** without JavaScript or additional CSS APIs. From a repository checkout run:

```sh
python3 examples/geo_operations_server.py --port 8765
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. It composes the existing `syntyr.core.css`, `syntyr.recipes.css` and `syntyr.geo.css` files into a responsive inventory search, accessible results/inspector, and fictional map schematic. Map coordinates are **illustrative pixel percentages**, not geographic coordinates. The Python file is a **source-only reference** and is not included in the distributable release ZIP. The server binds to localhost and contains fictional in-memory records; it has no credentials, accounts, tenant isolation, authorization, persistence or booking capability. Never expose this sample on a public interface as a production service.

### District drill-down and selection: interaction contract

The optional server example uses **real, browser-native GET navigation** for a small fictional district facet. The new `district` select and district links share search, status and format filters. District counts are computed after those other filters but before choosing a district, so the number on each link represents the results it would show. There is no JavaScript filtering or hidden application state.

| User action | Native UI and URL state | What the server must guarantee |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apply filters | Labeled `search` input and `select` controls, `method="get"` | Filter the **list and the schematic markers** from the same result set, recompute summary/counts and prevent stale selected records |
| Browse a district | Named `nav` of ordinary links with one `aria-current="page"` | Retain search, status and format; reset selection before choosing the first visible item |
| Select a map marker or an asset | Link with preserved filters and `selected=ID#selection` | Inspect only an asset that belongs to the currently filtered district; never reveal an out-of-scope record |
| Find a map marker from a record | `#map-marker-ID` points to a real named anchor | Preserve a keyboard-reachable target even with JavaScript disabled; do **not** pretend to center a real map camera |
| No matching records | Plain-text status with no markers or inspector | Clear stale selection and display an actionable filter-reset path |

This contract is **read-only demonstration behavior**, not tenant authorization. The district names and percentages are fictional, not geographic boundaries. A production application must validate parameters and permissions at the data-access layer, rather than treating filtered HTML or the marker list as an access-control boundary. Do not use the diagram's percentage coordinates to simulate real GIS geography.

Maintainers can optionally verify Chromium/Firefox native GET interaction, district navigation, 320px reflow, enlarged text, RTL markers and forced colors with `node tests/geo_operations_server_browser.cjs` after installing Playwright **outside** the Syntyr runtime. The script starts and shuts down the localhost Python server automatically. This does not replace manual screen-reader or real browser-zoom review.

## The boundary: cartographic behavior is an application concern

**Syntyr does not** calculate geographic coordinates, distances, bearings, geodesics, clustering, projections, antimeridian handling, routing or point-in-polygon queries. It cannot fetch or display basemap data, style vector tiles, perform hit testing, handle map keyboard navigation, or ensure geospatial measurement accuracy. Supply your own GIS data, map engine, and attribution. Syntyr only styles HTML around the actual map.

For interactive maps, integrate an engine such as [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/) (vector tiles / WebGL), [Leaflet](https://leafletjs.com/reference) (lightweight tiled/DOM maps), or [OpenLayers](https://openlayers.org/) (specialized GIS interactions and projections). They are **application dependencies**, not dependencies of Syntyr. Engine-native attribution and copyright/license requirements still apply; never remove provider credits. A decorative CSS attribution surface cannot replace legally required renderer attribution.

Choose and disclose the projection and coordinate reference system that your data needs (for example WGS 84 longitude/latitude for position inputs); do not assume a visual pixel distance equals a ground distance. Compute scale from the actual renderer viewport, latitude and zoom. Only set `data-syn-measured="true"` on `.syn-geo-scale` when the application has supplied a truthful measured label and bar length. Static examples deliberately say “Not to scale.”

## A map-ready, responsive shell

```html
<section class="syn-root syn-geo-shell" data-syn-theme="studio">
  <div class="syn-geo-workspace">
    <aside class="syn-geo-sidebar" aria-labelledby="locations-title">
      <h2 id="locations-title">Locations</h2>
      <ul class="syn-geo-data-list">
        <li><a href="#location-1">Site M-12 — operational</a></li>
      </ul>
    </aside>

    <div class="syn-geo-viewport" role="region"
         aria-label="Interactive site map; location details are also in the list">
      <div id="site-map" class="syn-geo-map"></div>
      <div class="syn-geo-overlay">
        <!-- Optional app-owned, functional controls and legend go here. -->
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>
```

The map mount fills the viewport, while `.syn-geo-overlay` lets pointer events pass through to the renderer except on Syntyr controls, legends and other interactive children. The workspace uses a **named container query** (`syn-geo`), so it stacks at narrow *container* sizes, including in a split dashboard. Set `--syn-geo-height`, `--syn-geo-compact-height` and `--syn-geo-sidebar-width` on an ancestor to customize its dimensions.

### Markers: use the renderer to position them

`.syn-geo-marker` styles a 44 × 44 CSS-pixel target with a smaller visible glyph. With MapLibre, provide a real native `button` to `new maplibregl.Marker({ element: button })`, then set the exact `LngLat` using `.setLngLat([longitude, latitude]).addTo(map)`. MapLibre owns the marker's geographic positioning; **do not place engine-managed marker elements inside `.syn-geo-marker-layer`**.

The pure HTML demo instead places links within `.syn-geo-marker-layer`; only those children use `--syn-geo-x` and `--syn-geo-y` for *diagram* coordinates, not GIS coordinates. These CSS percentages are expressly not a geographic coordinate API.

Use `data-syn-geo-kind="route"` for square markers or `"zone"` for rotated-square markers; ordinary sites remain round. `data-syn-selected="true"` and `aria-current="location"` provide a visible selection ring. `.syn-geo-cluster` styles an already-computed cluster count; **Syntyr never computes clustering**. An app must wire marker activation and popups, synchronize selection with the detail panel, and support keyboard navigation.

### Map controls and overlays

- `.syn-geo-controls`, `.syn-geo-control-group`, `.syn-geo-control` style the application's real `button` controls. A displayed control must work: wire zoom/pan to the map SDK, otherwise disable it.
- `.syn-geo-bottom`, `.syn-geo-legend`, `.syn-geo-legend-list`, `.syn-geo-swatch` style legends for points, routes, and zones. Always include text labels; swatch shape must not be the only source of meaning.
- `.syn-geo-callout` styles the body of an engine-positioned popup. Use safe DOM APIs and text nodes for untrusted feature labels instead of passing unsafe strings into HTML.
- `.syn-geo-scale` presents a scale label. A measured bar only appears for `data-syn-measured="true"` and a renderer-provided `--syn-geo-scale-length`.
- `.syn-geo-attribution` is a surface treatment for attribution you supply, not a replacement for engine-provided credits.
- `.syn-geo-layer-list` styles labeled checkboxes; connect state to the renderer's visible layer set. Checking a box alone does not change map data.
- `.syn-geo-data-list` provides a navigable, semantic fallback for locations and map features.

MapLibre and Leaflet already offer their own zoom, scale and attribution controls. Prefer their functional native versions instead of overlaying duplicate, inert Syntyr controls. Avoid covering copyright or the map's navigation affordances.

## Theming and accessibility

All seven Syntyr palettes resolve the nested tokens `--syn-geo-land`, `--syn-geo-water`, `--syn-geo-road`, `--syn-geo-parcel`, `--syn-geo-point`, `--syn-geo-route` and `--syn-geo-zone`, as well as `--syn-geo-floating`. These are UI/documentation defaults, **not** standardized GIS symbology, hazard categories or validated cartographic color scales. In a real map, assign purpose-specific and contrast-checked symbology to rendered geospatial layers.

For screen reader access, keep the meaningful asset list, labels, live states and a real HTML table or equivalent structured alternative **outside** the map canvas. Give every interactive marker an accessible name, make popup actions usable via keyboard, show an explicit focus ring, and announce state changes where appropriate. SVG diagrams used only as illustration may be `aria-hidden="true"` when the same information exists in text. Do not rely on hue alone for status or selection.

Touch targets are at least 44 CSS pixels in the provided controls and markers. Reflow should be audited at 320px and 400% zoom; verify that map overlays do not obscure attribution or details. Forced-colors users get native system-color surfaces and selected-marker outlines. Reduced-motion settings should also be respected by the **map renderer**, including camera transitions and animated geospatial layers.

## Product fit

Geo deliberately stays in its own CSS module rather than bloating core. Use it for OOH asset inventory maps, real-estate site selection, logistics fleet screens, field operations, municipal dashboards, parcel analysis and geospatial intelligence consoles. Any paid Syntyr Pro templates can compose this free MIT foundation while keeping premium implementation, integrations and domain-specific workflows in a separate licensed product.

## Optional real-MapLibre browser smoke (maintainers)

The repository also includes an intentionally **unpublished, developer-only** MapLibre integration fixture and browser harness. It loads locally installed MapLibre, Playwright and esbuild from a separate host application and bundles them for a temporary localhost page with a **synthetic offline map style**, no external tiles, credentials or real asset data. It is not the Syntyr runtime.

The [fixture HTML](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/tests/fixtures/geo-maplibre.html) and [application-owned wiring](https://github.com/dporkka/syntyr-css/blob/main/tests/fixtures/geo-maplibre-app.js) demonstrate the complete **map ↔ list ↔ inspector** contract with three fictional longitude/latitude points:

1. The native list links navigate to a real, focusable details section. MapLibre-owned marker **buttons** expose accessible names; Enter and Space select the same record.
2. The host app updates exactly one selected record in the list, selected-marker ring, inspector and polite status announcement. List selection calls MapLibre `map.jumpTo({center: ...})`, using real `LngLat` positions and the renderer's projection, not `--syn-geo-x` or CSS percentage coordinates.
3. Native status and search controls update both the list and actual MapLibre markers. A hidden/unknown record cannot be selected through the example UI; no-results states clear the inspector and selected markers. Returning to a broader filter keeps the current selection **if it remains visible**.
4. The fixture starts with filters and zoom **disabled** until the app wires their behavior. Without JavaScript, the authored list, initial details and explicit `noscript` explanation remain readable; the list only becomes clickable once the application has wired selection, so it never links inactive sites to unrelated details.
5. Browser checks validate real geographic marker projection, zoom, marker/list keyboard activation, selection and empty-state consistency, 44px targets, mobile container reflow, overlay pointer events, 2×/4× root-font stress, forced colors and reduced motion.

**Authorization boundary:** this is *not* a security implementation. The three fictional points are embedded in test-only JavaScript and are all visible to anyone with the fixture. Client-side filtering and rejecting unknown UI selections do **not** provide authentication, tenant isolation, feature authorization or data privacy. A real OOH/map application must deliver only server-authorized records, enforce per-record and per-tenant permissions at each API or tile endpoint, and verify selection/detail requests server-side. Never load sensitive cross-tenant assets and hope CSS, map layers, or browser filtering hide them. Do not use this synthetic test as evidence that real tenant isolation is working.

**Host-owned design decision:** the fixture uses safe `textContent` updates instead of interpolating record names into `innerHTML`, `map.jumpTo` instead of simulated CSS marker placement, and ordinary browser focus/fragment navigation instead of a custom focus trap. Other applications can use React, HTMX, or plain JavaScript for this orchestration; Syntyr only supplies the optional geospatial presentation styles.

~~~sh
SYNTYR_VENDOR_NODE_MODULES=/path/to/installed/node_modules \
  node tests/geo_maplibre_browser.mjs
~~~

Set `SYNTYR_GEO_CHROMIUM_PATH` if the locally installed Playwright browser revision differs from Playwright's default, or `SYNTYR_GEO_SCREENSHOT_DIR` to save developer-only screenshots. The harness never runs as a Syntyr consumer dependency. Its static fixture and scripts are **not** published on Cloudflare or in the release ZIP.

**Adacavo integration decision:** prefer borrowing Syntyr Geo layout, legend and accessible map-chrome patterns into the existing MapLibre inventory view **without importing an unreleased Syntyr CSS package**. Retain Adacavo's tenant-safe APIs, actual inventory status colors, source clustering, positioning, map controls and map attribution. Reevaluate package-level integration only after Syntyr's CSS is released and proven stable.
